papers.abstract_en: Metastasis remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality, a process in which circulating tumor cells (CTCs) play a central but incompletely understood role. Although most CTCs are rapidly eliminated during circulation through detachment-induced anoikis and fluid shear stress (SS)-triggered apoptosis, a subset of CTCs can survive these hostile conditions; however, the underlying mechanisms remain poorly defined. To investigate this, we developed a microfluidic circulatory system that mimics physiological SS and performed transcriptomic profiling of A549 lung cancer cells under SS, attached, and static suspension conditions. Through this approach, we identified the ROS-CD44-Ezrin axis as a potential mechanosignaling module that may contribute to CTC survival under shear stress. In this cascade, SS-induced ROS and CD44 converge to activate Ezrin via phosphorylation at Thr567. Once activated, Ezrin appears to coordinate its two canonical functions-membrane-cytoskeleton reinforcement and pro-survival signaling via PI3K/AKT/Bcl-2 and NF-κB/p38/JNK pathways-within this specific mechanobiological context to preserve cell integrity and limit apoptosis. Our findings suggest that these well-established molecular functions are differentially engaged under shear stress, revealing a context-dependent survival mechanism that may offer opportunities for therapeutic exploration, pending further validation in more clinically relevant models.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: The malignant progression of nonsmall cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is closely related to cancer stemness. Histone deacetylase 4 (HDAC4) plays a regulatory role in lung cancer, but its effect on NSCLC stemness remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the role and mechanism of HDAC4 in NSCLC stemness. METHODS: In this study, a tumor-bearing model was established by subcutaneously injecting A549 cells into the right dorsal side of nude mice. Reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR), Western blotting, and immunohistochemistry were used to measure gene and protein expression levels. Flow cytometry, sphere formation assays, and Transwell experiments were employed to assess cancer cell stemness, migration, and invasion. Additionally, a kit was used to measure changes in glutamine metabolism-related indicators. RESULTS: In this study, we found that knocking down HDAC4 expression inhibited the expression of SRY-box transcription factor 2 (SOX2), octamer-binding transcription factor 4 (OCT4), and nanog homeobox (NANOG) in A549 cells; it also reduced the proportions of CD133- and CD44-positive cells and suppressed their sphere formation, cell migration, and invasion abilities. Furthermore, HDAC4 knockdown inhibited glutamine uptake, glutamate production, α-ketoglutarate levels, and glutaminase (GLS) activity. Notably, treatment with the additional glutamine metabolism inhibitor CB-839 attenuated the promoting effects of HDAC4 overexpression on the stemness, migration, and invasion of A549 cells. In addition, HDAC4 promoted the expression of hypoxia-inducible factor-1 alpha (HIF-1α) and solute carrier family 38 member 2 (SLC38A2); after overexpressing HIF-1α, the inhibitory effect of HDAC4 knockdown on SLC38A2 expression in A549 cells was weakened. CONCLUSION: Our study reveals a critical mechanism by which HDAC4 enhances glutamine metabolism through upregulation of HIF-1α expression to promote SLC38A2 expression, thereby driving NSCLC stemness and progression.

papers.abstract_en: Drug therapies targeting vasculature in metastatic cancer have not been highly effective and are therefore currently limited to an adjunctive role, such as in combination regimens. The development of novel, more effective therapeutic strategies with new mechanisms of action is therefore greatly needed. In a previous study, we reported a lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-based vascular-disrupting strategy utilizing cyclic RGD peptide-modified LNPs encapsulating small interfering RNA against Fas ligand (cRGD-LNP/siFasL). We combined this strategy for selective targeting of tumor endothelial cells with stimulator of interferon genes (STING) agonist-loaded LNPs (STING-LNPs). Here, we have demonstrated the potential of such combination therapy in treating lung metastases. We found that cRGD-LNPs accumulated in the vasculature within tumor colonies in the lung. A combination of cRGD-LNP/siFasL and STING-LNP induced significant antitumor effects in mouse models of Renca and 4T1 lung metastases. Moreover, this combination therapy reduced the vasculature within tumor colonies, with no obvious change in the surrounding normal lung tissue, indicating preferential vascular disruption. These findings demonstrate that the combination therapy exerts antitumor activity against lung metastases through tumor vascular disruption, indicating that such treatment is potentially a potent disrupter of the vascularity in metastatic tumors.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVE: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are essential in the modulation of cellular activities. Studies suggest that miR-3615 may possess a tumour-suppressive function in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD); however, its precise role and molecular mechanisms in LUAD progression remain incompletely understood. The aim of the study is to systematically investigate the biological functions and underlying mechanisms of miR-3615 in LUAD. MATERIAL AND METHODS: The expression of miR-3615 in LUAD cell lines was quantified by real-time quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR). Subsequently, its functional effects on proliferation, migration, invasion, and apoptosis were evaluated in A549 and H1299 cells using the CCK-8 assay, Transwell assay, and flow cytometry, respectively. Potential target genes of miR-3615 were predicted and functionally annotated using bioinformatics methods. The binding interaction of miR-3615 with the CALML4 gene was demonstrated via a dual-luciferase reporter assay. RESULTS: miR-3615 expression was notably downregulated in LUAD cell lines compared with normal cells. Overexpression of miR-3615 inhibited the proliferation, migration, and invasion capabilities of LUAD cells while promoting apoptosis. Integrated bioinformatics analysis involving target prediction and functional enrichment identified CALML4 as a key candidate target gene of miR-3615. CALML4 was confirmed as a direct target of miR-3615. The effects of miR-3615 mimic on LUAD cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and apoptosis were partly attenuated by CALML4 overexpression. CONCLUSIONS: miR-3615 exerts its functional impact on LUAD cells by directly downregulating CALML4, thereby curbing proliferation, migration, and invasion and promoting apoptosis. The elucidated miR-3615/CALML4 axis advances the theoretical foundation for studying LUAD development.

papers.abstract_en: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have revolutionised the management of advanced malignancies, but can cause immune-related adverse events (irAEs), including vision-threatening complications such as optic neuropathy. Ocular irAEs have been described with several programmed death-1/programmed death-ligand 1 and cytotoxic T lymphocyte-associated antigen-4 inhibitors, but ocular toxicities of tislelizumab have so far been limited to Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada (VKH)-like uveitis, panuveitis and retinal vasculitis. We describe a woman with metastatic lung adenocarcinoma who was treated with second-line gemcitabine, carboplatin and tislelizumab. After the second cycle of chemo-immunotherapy, she developed painless, progressive bilateral visual blurring in the absence of intracranial disease. Ophthalmic assessment was consistent with toxic optic neuropathy in the context of ongoing tislelizumab exposure, and other causes were excluded. Tislelizumab was discontinued and high-dose intravenous methylprednisolone (1 g/day for 5 days) was administered, without ICI re-challenge. Visual function did not improve, indicating an irreversible optic nerve injury. To our knowledge, this is the first reported case of toxic optic neuropathy associated with tislelizumab, extending the spectrum of tislelizumab-related ocular irAEs beyond previously documented VKH-like panuveitis, VKH-like uveitis and retinal vasculitis. This case highlights the importance of early recognition of visual symptoms and periodic ophthalmic assessment in patients receiving ICIs, as well as decision-making regarding ICI continuation or discontinuation when sight-threatening neuro-ophthalmic irAEs are suspected.

papers.abstract_en: Lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) is an aggressive malignancy with a poor prognosis. Given the association between mitochondrial dysregulation and LUSC, the aim of the present study was to identify mitochondrial unfolded protein response (UPRmt)‑related candidate genes associated with LUSC and to explore their potential functional relevance. In the present study, differential expression, univariate Cox and survival analyses were combined to identify a UPRmt‑associated key gene in LUSC. Gene set enrichment analysis was then performed, and overexpression (OE) and knockdown cell lines were used to clarify its function using western blotting, Cell Counting Kit‑8, colony formation and Transwell® invasion assays. Using bioinformatics tools and a review of the literature, PTEN‑induced kinase 1 (PINK1) was singled out as a key gene in LUSC samples. Elevated PINK1 expression was associated with worse survival outcomes. A total of 117 pathways were enriched by PINK1, with the top 5 including 'focal adhesion' and 'mitogen‑activated protein kinase signaling pathway'. Using experimental analysis, it was observed that PINK1 significantly enhanced the proliferative, migratory, invasive and colony forming abilities of tumor cells, thereby exacerbating LUSC. Furthermore, these enhancements were diminished by the application of focal adhesion kinase (FAK) inhibitor. It was also noted that the expression levels of protein kinase B (AKT), p‑AKT, Ras homolog family member A (RhoA) and vinculin were all elevated in OE‑PINK1 cells. Collectively, these findings indicated that PINK1 exerted its influence on LUSC through the FAK/AKT/RhoA/vinculin pathway. The present study identified PINK1 as a key gene in LUSC, exerting its influence through the FAK/AKT/RhoA/vinculin pathway, thereby presenting a potential novel therapeutic target for the treatment of LUSC in the future.

papers.abstract_en: Burkholderia pseudomallei, the causative agent of melioidosis, is a gram-negative bacterium historically endemic to Southeast Asia and Northern Australia. However, recent environmental detection along the Gulf Coast and an increasing number of reported cases in non-travelers have raised questions regarding potential endemicity and environmental establishment in the Southern United States. We report a case of putatively locally acquired pulmonary melioidosis in a Florida resident with no recent international travel history, illustrating the diagnostic and therapeutic challenges posed by this rare pathogen. The patient presented with fever, pleuritic chest pain, and hypoxia following a period of severe weather. Computed tomography (CT) of the chest revealed multiple solid pulmonary nodules with ground-glass opacities and mediastinal lymphadenopathy. Given his underlying stage 3b chronic kidney disease (CKD), the patient was treated with an intensive course of intravenous ceftazidime followed by oral doxycycline monotherapy, achieving full clinical recovery. Follow-up imaging at 3 months demonstrated complete resolution of the pulmonary nodules. This case emphasizes the importance of considering melioidosis in the differential diagnosis for non-resolving community-acquired pneumonia or significant pulmonary nodules in the Southern United States, even in the absence of international travel. Risk factors such as diabetes mellitus and severe weather events are key clinical clues. While trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole remains the preferred eradication therapy, doxycycline may serve as a potential alternative for patients with renal impairment when first-line therapy is contraindicated.

papers.authors: Mahdi ZA, AlmjalawI BSA, Naimuzzaman M, Hasan MM, Kumer A, Al-Alaq FT, Al-Dahmoshi HOM, Rahman F et al.

papers.abstract_en: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, with a five-year survival rate of approximately 20-25% despite advances in targeted therapy and immunotherapy. There is a continuous need for novel, low-toxicity compounds capable of modulating key oncogenic pathways in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Mangrove ecosystems are rich reservoirs of bioactive phytochemicals, yet the inhibitory potential of compounds from Rhizophora mucronata against validated lung cancer-associated proteins has not been systematically explored using multi-scale computational approaches. This study employed an integrated computational pipeline to evaluate 14 phytochemicals from R. mucronata. Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations at the B3LYP/6-31G* level were performed to characterize electronic properties of the ligands. Molecular docking studies were conducted using both AutoDock Vina (PyRx) and Schrödinger Glide against the Keap1 Kelch domain (PDB 1X2J) and the YEATS2 YEATS domain (PDB 5XNV). Top-ranked complexes were subjected to 100-ns molecular dynamics (MD) simulations in Desmond, and pharmacokinetic and toxicity profiles were predicted using SwissADME and pkCSM. Among the screened compounds, ligand L10 (cyclohexane-1,2,3,4,5,6-hexaol) exhibited the smallest HOMO-LUMO energy gap (0.36 eV), favorable binding affinities (Glide score of -7.789 kcal/mol against 1X2J), multiple hydrogen-bonding interactions, and stable complex behavior during MD simulations (Cα RMSD < 3 Å). Several other ligands (L02, L05, and L07) also displayed promising profiles. Most compounds complied with Lipinski's rule of five and showed acceptable predicted ADMET properties. These preliminary findings suggest that Rhizophora mucronate -derived phytochemicals, particularly L10, are promising candidates for further experimental evaluation as modulators of Keap1 and YEATS2 in lung cancer. This study provides a computational framework for prioritizing natural product leads from mangrove species for subsequent in vitro and in vivo validation.

papers.authors_conclusion: 我们提出，可塑性最宜被理解为一种耦联的调控状态，源于致癌背景、染色质控制与代谢支持之间的相互作用；界定这些依赖如何产生并在高可塑性过渡态中形成功能耦联，应有助于识别在替代谱系程序稳定之前拦截谱系转换的切入点。

papers.abstract_en: Cellular plasticity is a central feature of malignant progression, allowing tumour cells to change identity during tumour evolution, therapeutic adaptation, and metastatic dissemination. This issue is especially acute in lung cancer, where the respiratory epithelium is intrinsically permissive to cell-state change. Genetic lesions, chromatin regulation, and metabolic adaptation are often framed as parallel determinants of lineage plasticity. Emerging evidence instead points to functional coupling across these layers. Oncogenic alterations can weaken lineage fidelity and open alternative trajectories, chromatin regulators can stabilise transitional states and enforce new transcriptional programmes, and metabolic rewiring can supply the biochemical conditions required for these states to emerge and persist. Microenvironmental cues further influence which trajectories are selected and maintained. Here, we discuss the genetic, epigenetic, and metabolic determinants of lineage plasticity in lung cancer, focusing on the points at which they intersect. We propose that plasticity is most usefully understood as a coupled regulatory state, arising from the interaction between oncogenic context, chromatin control, and metabolic support. Defining how these dependencies arise and become functionally coupled within high-plasticity transitional states should help identify points at which lineage switching can be intercepted before alternative lineage programmes are stabilised.

papers.abstract_en: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) remains the most aggressive form of breast cancer with a worse prognosis than other subtypes. Its high metastatic potential, limited availability of targeted therapies, and increased likelihood of being diagnosed at an advanced stage make it one of the most complex clinical challenges in breast cancer. Today, thanks to the advent of antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), clinical outcomes have improved significantly. In this context, sacituzumab govitecan (SG) has been a true revolution. The case reported here illustrates how this therapeutic opportunity produced lasting clinical benefit in a highly complex patient with a triple neoplasm at presentation: inoperable locally advanced TNBC, operable colon cancer, and localized lung cancer. The chemorefractory patient (rapid progression of the first two lines of chemotherapy) received SG as a third-line treatment, showing a sustained response lasting more than 12 months and a significant benefit in terms of quality of life. This case highlights how a proper multidisciplinary approach can lead to a lasting clinical benefit from therapy. Deviating from the cases reported in clinical studies, it is important to underscore how, in this context, clinical choice prevailed. Given the locally advanced stage of the breast cancer, characterized by carcinomatous mastitis tending to ulceration and the high proliferation rate, compared to the localized stage of lung adenocarcinoma, a multidisciplinary decision was made to treat the more rapidly progressing disease, TNBC. In light of this, the importance of collecting clinical practice data to support the complex challenges we face daily is emphasized.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to investigate the relationship between the lung and bronchus cancer incidence rate, the lung and bronchus cancer mortality rate, economic growth, health expenditures, and environmental degradation using data from US states. METHODS: In the study, the cointegration and causality relationships among the time series data were examined. The autoregressive distributed lag (ARDL) bounds test was used to estimate the short- and long-term coefficients of the variables representing lung and bronchus cancer incidence bronchus and mortality rates, economic growth, health expenditures, and environmental degradation variables. The data used in the study cover the annual period from 1999 through 2020. RESULTS: According to the ARDL bounds test results, economic growth and environmental degradation increased lung and bronchus cancer incidence mortality rates, while health expenditures reduced them. Causality tests indicated that economic growth unidirectionally affected lung and bronchus cancer incidence and mortality rates and environmental degradation. The results of other causality tests are presented in the conclusion section. CONCLUSION: Based on the findings, it is recommended to implement policies that reduce environmental degradation without hindering economic growth. By implementing such policies, cancer incidence and mortality rates may decrease, and at the same time, public welfare may increase. Policymakers should make decisions that advance both economic and human health objectives.

papers.abstract_en: We present the case of a woman in her 30s presenting in the second trimester with frank haematuria and left flank discomfort. MRI revealed a T3b bladder tumour with suspected peritoneal invasion. Chemotherapy was contraindicated due to teratogenicity. A coordinated obstetrics-urology MDT was undertaken at 33 weeks, an elective caesarean section was performed immediately followed by a transurethral resection of bladder for tumour debulking and histological assessment. A preterm but healthy infant was delivered and subsequently discharged from NICU. Histology revealed grade 2 bladder adenocarcinoma, in keeping with urachal origin. The patient progressed to metastatic T4 disease with pulmonary metastases and peritoneal involvement, requiring palliative chemotherapy. This case underscores the importance of a multidisciplinary approach in managing advanced bladder cancer during pregnancy, balancing maternal and foetal safety, respecting patient preferences and optimising oncological outcomes while highlighting the diagnostic and therapeutic challenges of cancer diagnosis in pregnancy.

papers.abstract_en: A man in his late 70s presented with progressive, painless scrotal swelling. The initial ultrasound was reported as a simple hydrocele, and he was scheduled for surgery. At operation, friable nodules on the tunica vaginalis were biopsied, confirming malignant epithelioid mesothelioma. Staging CT showed no pleural or peritoneal disease, supporting a primary tunica vaginalis origin. As the tunica vaginalis is an embryological continuation of the peritoneum, it is exceptionally rare for mesothelioma to arise here as a true primary rather than as a secondary spread from the peritoneum. This case highlights a rare primary malignant mesothelioma masquerading as a hydrocele, the limitations of ultrasound as a sole diagnostic tool and the importance of maintaining suspicion when operative findings are discordant with imaging.

papers.abstract_en: The European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Clinical Practice Guidelines for the diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of patients with early and locally advanced non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) were published in August 2025 and were adapted in November 2025 according to previously established standard methodology to produce the Pan-Asian adapted ESMO consensus guidelines for the management of Asian patients with early and locally advanced NSCLC. The adapted guidelines presented in this article represent the consensus opinions reached by a panel of Asian experts on the treatment of patients with early and locally advanced NSCLC representing the oncological societies of China (Chinese Society of Clinical Oncology), Indonesia (Indonesian Society of Hematology and Medical Oncology), India (Indian Society of Medical and Paediatric Oncology), Japan [Japanese Society of Medical Oncology (JSMO)], South Korea (Korean Society of Medical Oncology), Malaysia (Malaysian Oncological Society), the Philippines (Philippine Society of Medical Oncology), Singapore (Singapore Society of Oncology), Taiwan (Taiwan Oncology Society) and Thailand (Thai Society of Clinical Oncology), coordinated by ESMO and JSMO. The voting was based on scientific evidence and was independent of the current treatment practices, drug access restrictions and reimbursement decisions in the different regions of Asia. The latter are discussed separately in the article. The aim is to provide guidance for the optimisation and harmonisation of the management of patients with early and locally advanced NSCLC across the different countries of Asia, drawing on the evidence provided by both Western and Asian trials. Attention is drawn to the disparity in the drug approvals and reimbursement strategies among the different regions.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy has become the standard-of-care for stage II-III triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC); however, anthracycline-containing regimens are associated with considerable toxicity. We evaluated camrelizumab combined with an anthracycline-free docetaxel-carboplatin regimen in this setting. PATIENTS AND METHODS: We performed a multicenter, randomized, open-label, phase 3 trial at 14 hospitals in China between December 2022 and June 2025. Eligible patients were women aged 18-70 years with previously untreated, stage II-III TNBC. Patients were randomized 2:1 to receive 6 cycles of neoadjuvant docetaxel (75 mg/m2) plus carboplatin (area under the curve [AUC]=6) on day 1, with or without camrelizumab (200 mg intravenously on day 3). The primary endpoint was pathological complete response (pCR), defined as ypT0/Tis ypN0, evaluated in the modified intention-to-treat (mITT) population (all patients who received at least one dose of study treatment). RESULTS: A total of 369 patients were enrolled, and 352 comprised the mITT population for efficacy analysis. The pCR rate was 57.5% (134/233) in the camrelizumab-chemotherapy group and 45.4% (54/119) in the chemotherapy-alone group, corresponding to an absolute difference of 12.2% (95% CI, 1.4 to 22.9; one-sided P=0.014). Grade 3-4 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 24.9% (58/233) in the camrelizumab-chemotherapy group and 21.8% (26/119) in the chemotherapy-alone group. No treatment-related deaths were reported. CONCLUSION: The addition of camrelizumab to neoadjuvant docetaxel plus carboplatin significantly increased the pCR rate in patients with stage II-III TNBC, with a manageable safety profile. This regimen represents a promising anthracycline-free strategy that warrants comparison with current standard chemoimmunotherapy .

papers.abstract_en: IMPORTANCE: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) with inferior vena cava (IVC) tumor thrombus is associated with substantial perioperative risk and frequent recurrence despite nephrectomy and thrombectomy. No established neoadjuvant local therapy exists for this high-risk population. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the feasibility, safety, clinical outcomes, and exploratory biomarker effects of neoadjuvant stereotactic ablative radiotherapy (SABR) targeting IVC tumor thrombus before nephrectomy and thrombectomy. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This single-center prospective phase 2 nonrandomized clinical trial enrolled patients with newly diagnosed RCC and Mayo level II to IV IVC tumor thrombus eligible for neoadjuvant SABR and definitive surgery from July 2015 to January 2024. Data were analyzed from August 2025 to August 2026. INTERVENTION: Neoadjuvant SABR to the radiographically defined IVC tumor thrombus, delivered as 40 Gy in 5 fractions or 36 Gy in 3 fractions, followed by radical nephrectomy and IVC thrombectomy. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary end point was 1-year recurrence-free survival (RFS) compared with a prespecified historical surgery-alone benchmark of 55.7%. Secondary outcomes included 90-day perioperative morbidity and mortality, adverse events, pulmonary embolism, overall survival, and cancer-specific survival. Exploratory analyses included Ki-67 immunohistochemistry and tumor-informed circulating tumor DNA. RESULTS: Of 23 patients who received neoadjuvant SABR, 22 completed surgery, and 21 were included in the primary RFS analysis. Of 21 included patients, 12 (57%) were male, and the median (IQR) age was 62.5 (54.0-73.2) years. A total of 19 patients had clear-cell RCC; all tumors were grade 3 or 4, and 3 patients had metastatic disease at enrollment. At a median (range) follow-up of 108.6 (2.0-127.2) months, 1-year RFS was 71.4% (80% CI, 56.6-82.0; 95% CI, 47.2-86.0), meeting the prespecified phase 2 screening criterion based on comparison with the historical surgery-alone benchmark of 55.7% (P = .09). One-year overall survival was 95.2% (80% CI, 83.9-98.7; 95% CI, 70.7-99.3) and cancer-specific survival was 95.2% (80% CI, 83.9-98.7; 95% CI, 70.7-99.3). No 90-day perioperative mortality occurred; 4 grade 4 treatment-attributed events occurred, but no grade 4/5 radiation-attributed toxic effects occurred. Ki-67 expression was reduced in patients with irradiated tumor thrombus compared with nonirradiated controls. Tumor-informed circulating tumor DNA was detected in all patients with available plasma and declined after treatment. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this nonrandomized clinical trial, neoadjuvant SABR before nephrectomy and IVC thrombectomy appeared feasible with an acceptable safety profile. RFS met the prespecified phase 2 screening criterion but remains exploratory and warrants further evaluation. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT02473536.

papers.abstract_en: IMPORTANCE: Neoadjuvant nivolumab plus ipilimumab in localized deficient mismatch repair/microsatellite instability-high gastric or gastroesophageal junction (GEJ) adenocarcinoma was evaluated in the NEONIPIGA study. The primary end point of pathological complete response (pCR) was previously reported. OBJECTIVE: To report long-term follow-up results and secondary end points, including event-free survival (EFS) and overall survival (OS), of the NEONIPIGA study. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: The NEONIPIGA study is a French, multicenter, single-arm, phase 2 nonrandomized clinical trial that included patients with histologically proven cT2-T4NXM0 deficient mismatch repair/microsatellite instability-high GEJ adenocarcinoma who were eligible for surgery. Patients were enrolled between October 23, 2019, and June 4, 2021, and the database was locked on November 13, 2025. INTERVENTION: Neoadjuvant nivolumab, 240 mg, every 2 weeks for 6 cycles plus ipilimumab, 1 mg/kg, every 6 weeks for 2 cycles, followed by surgery 5 weeks after the last nivolumab dose, and adjuvant nivolumab, 480 mg, every 4 weeks for 9 cycles. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: EFS and OS. RESULTS: A total of 32 patients (median [range] age, 65 [40-80] years; 8 [28%] female and 21 [72%] were male) were included: 16 (50%) with gastric cancer and 16 (50%) with GEJ cancer. Three patients did not undergo surgery (1 with metastatic disease and 2 who refused). Twenty-seven patients (84%) completed neoadjuvant therapy and 14 (44%) received all treatment as planned. Neoadjuvant and adjuvant therapy-related grade 3/4 adverse events occurred in 6 (19%) and 4 patients (17%), respectively. Median follow-up was 48.3 months (95% CI, 44.8-52.0 months). Among the 32 patients in the intention-to-treat population, 4-year OS was 84.1% (95% CI, 65.8%-93.0%). In the 31 patients eligible for surgery, 4-year EFS was 83.5% (95% CI, 64.8%-92.8%). One patient relapsed with cerebral metastases. Six deaths occurred: 2 related to gastric cancer or treatment (1 patient had postoperative complications and 1 cerebral metastases) and 4 unrelated. All patients who did not undergo surgery achieved a clinical complete response after immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy. One patient subsequently died of causes unrelated to their cancer. Overall, 17 of 29 patients (59%) achieved pCR on surgical specimen. Safety was previously reported, and no additional late toxic effects were observed. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this phase 2 nonrandomized clinical trial, the immunotherapy regimen evaluated was associated with sustained long-term survival, but no clear evidence of improved survival over outcomes reported in other studies evaluating surgery alone in this patient population was observed. The high pCR rates and durable responses observed may provide useful information for designing future clinical studies, including randomized trials investigating organ-preserving strategies. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04006262.

papers.abstract_en: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have demonstrated substantial weight reduction and cardiometabolic benefit in randomized trials; however, prospective implementation evidence from digital care models and female sex community populations remains limited. Here we report outcomes from an observational study of 8,127 women initiating GLP-1RA therapy (99.8% tirzepatide) through a structured digital program incorporating mandatory biochemical monitoring, weekly video-supported follow-up and clinician-guided dose titration in the UK. Mean weight reduction was 16.1 kg (95% confidence interval 15.9 to 16.2; P < 0.001), representing 15.5% of baseline weight; 83.1% achieved ≥10% and 22.4% achieved ≥20% weight loss, with consistent responses across age, baseline weight and socioeconomic strata. Among participants with paired biomarker data, mean glycated hemoglobin decreased by 3.3 mmol mol-1 (95% confidence interval 3.1 to 3.4; P < 0.001), normalizing in 84.5% of those with baseline diabetes-range values and 96.3% with prediabetes, and lipid parameters improved significantly (reductions in total cholesterol of 0.77 mmol l-1, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol of 0.61 mmol l-1 and triglycerides of 0.47 mmol l-1). Retention was 91.4% at 6 months, with no serious treatment-related adverse events. These findings support the feasibility of delivering structured, digitally enabled obesity pharmacotherapy at scale and provide prospective real-world implementation evidence for this care model. Interpretation is limited by the observational design, absence of a comparator group, self-pay population and 6-month follow-up.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Endoscopic ultrasound (EUS)-guided drainage is the standard of care for walled-off necrosis (WON); however, the optimal timing of subsequent endoscopic necrosectomy remains uncertain. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing immediate versus on-demand necrosectomy following EUS-guided drainage. METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library through March 2026 for RCTs comparing immediate (≤ 72 h) versus on-demand necrosectomy in adults with necrotizing pancreatitis. Primary outcomes were technical success, clinical success, and the proportion of patients undergoing necrosectomy. Secondary outcomes included length of hospital stay, costs, need for percutaneous or multigate drainage, and adverse events. Pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using random-effects models. RESULTS: Four RCTs comprising 215 patients, of whom 192 (89.3%) had WON, were included. Immediate and on-demand approaches demonstrated similar technical success (RR 1.01, 95%CI 0.98-1.05) and clinical success (RR 1.17, 95%CI 0.98-1.40). Immediate necrosectomy was associated with a higher proportion of patients undergoing necrosectomy (RR 1.65, 95%CI 1.13-2.41). No significant differences were observed in length of hospital stay, costs, need for additional drainage, procedure- or disease-related adverse events, mortality, bleeding, stent migration, or pneumoperitoneum. CONCLUSIONS: Immediate endoscopic necrosectomy did not demonstrate a consistent clinical advantage over an on-demand approach. Low- to very-low-certainty evidence suggests little or no difference in clinical efficacy or safety outcomes, while very-low-certainty evidence suggests that immediate necrosectomy may increase the proportion of patients undergoing necrosectomy. However, the magnitude and clinical significance of this effect remain uncertain. These findings should be interpreted cautiously given the limited number of randomized trials, modest sample sizes, and low or very low certainty of evidence for several outcomes. TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261366884).

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) accounts for ~ 85% of lung cancers and is associated with poor outcomes in advanced stages. Radiotherapy (RT) is central to NSCLC treatment, yet locoregional relapse remains frequent. Increasing evidence indicates that, beyond tumor-intrinsic adaptations, the tumor microenvironment (TME) and immune contexture critically influence response to irradiation. However, most radioresistance models rely on human cell lines unsuitable for immunocompetent systems, limiting insight into immune-tumor interactions. METHODS: We generated radioresistant (RR) isogenic variants of murine lung adenocarcinoma cell lines and investigated RT resistance using transcriptomics, 3D co-culture systems, and syngeneic mouse models. RESULTS: RR clones showed stable adaptations to DNA damage, including enhanced clonogenic survival, reduced immunogenic cell death, and constitutive activation of DNA damage response pathways, particularly ATR signaling. High ATR levels in NSCLC patients were significantly associated with immunosuppression. Transcriptomics revealed altered DNA repair and downregulation of type-I interferon and innate immune pathways. In vivo, RR tumors exhibited an immunosuppressive TME with increased T regulatory cells, M2-like macrophages, and myeloid-derived suppressor cells, alongside reduced cytotoxic T cell recruitment. In 3D co-cultures, immunosuppressive cells protected cancer cells from RT-induced cytotoxicity. Notably, RR tumors regained RT sensitivity in immunodeficient mice, highlighting the role of immune suppression in radioresistance. Therapeutically, activation of innate immunity using TLR3-TLR7/8 agonists (poly(I:C)+R848) restored antitumor responses and improved RT efficacy, partly via CXCL9/10-mediated immune recruitment. ATR inhibition with ceralasertib further sensitized RR tumors to RT. CONCLUSION: These findings identify cancer cell-intrinsic ATR signaling and immune suppression as key drivers of radioresistance and support combined therapeutic strategies to prevent locoregional relapse in NSCLC after radiotherapy.

papers.results: 共纳入33项研究、3585例肺癌患者，其中26项为回顾性观察研究；30项研究以中轴骨（主要为脊柱转移）为主，仅6项包含附肢骨病灶（两类不互斥）。局部干预在部分筛选患者中与疼痛缓解、行走能力的维持或恢复、神经功能改善及局部症状控制相关；比较性生存结果不一致；未确立手术的因果性生存获益；并发症模式因干预类型而异；总体证据确定性为低至极低，附肢骨与骨盆病灶最弱。
papers.authors_conclusion: 骨科处理对保留功能、控制机械性或神经性并发症可能具有临床重要性，但脊柱病灶的证据明显强于脊柱外病灶；治疗应保持多学科与个体化；所提出的决策框架为概念性、基于指南的，而非经过验证的治疗算法。
papers.ai_note: 主要局限：33项研究中26项为回顾性设计，存在选择偏倚与适应证混杂（confounding by indication），因此“疼痛缓解、行走能力维持、神经功能改善”等表述仍属相关性而非疗效；未行定量合并，全部为叙述性综合，故无效应量与置信区间；“手术无因果生存获益”这一阴性结论建立在低至极低确定性证据之上，摘要同时以功能获益的正面表述呈现，存在结论口径上的张力；检索时间窗截至2025年12月，需核对与发表时点是否一致及是否注册（PROSPERO）。

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Bone metastases from lung cancer can cause pain, pathological fracture, spinal instability, metastatic spinal cord compression and loss of independence. Lung cancer-specific evidence for orthopaedically relevant local management remains fragmented. This review assessed outcomes across spinal, appendicular and pelvic skeletal disease, while explicitly examining the anatomical distribution and limitations of the evidence. METHODS: PubMed, Web of Science, Europe PMC and Scopus were searched for original studies published from January 2015 to December 2025. Eligible studies evaluated orthopaedic, surgical, minimally invasive or percutaneous skeletal interventions, including radiotherapy when combined with or directly compared with an orthopaedically relevant local strategy. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data and completed the full Joanna Briggs Institute checklist applicable to each design. Findings were synthesised narratively, with evidence certainty assessed using GRADE. RESULTS: Thirty-three studies comprising 3585 participants with lung cancer were included; 26 were retrospective observational studies. Thirty studies predominantly evaluated axial disease, mainly spinal metastases, whereas only six included appendicular lesions; these categories were not mutually exclusive. Local interventions were associated with pain relief, maintenance or recovery of ambulation, neurological improvement and local symptom control in selected patients. Comparative survival findings were inconsistent and vulnerable to selection bias and confounding by indication; no causal survival benefit of surgery was established. Complication patterns differed by intervention type. Overall certainty was low to very low and was weakest for appendicular and pelvic disease. CONCLUSIONS: Orthopaedic management can be clinically important for preserving function and controlling mechanical or neurological complications, but the evidence is substantially stronger for spinal than for extraspinal disease. Treatment should remain multidisciplinary and individualised. The proposed decision frameworks are conceptual and guideline-informed rather than validated treatment algorithms.

papers.abstract_en: Breast cancer that arises in the postpartum period often carries a poor prognosis and urgently requires chemoprevention strategies, particularly for women at elevated risk. Here, we report that a single post-lactation dose of cabergoline, a dopaminergic agonist that blocks prolactin secretion, delays the onset and reduces the incidence of postpartum mammary cancer in K14-Cre; Brca1F/F, Trp53F/F mice. In these mice, cabergoline treatment remodels the mammary gland by potentiating involution, reducing ductal area and proliferation, and reversing T cell exhaustion, potentially through modulation of ion channel expression. Notably, independent retrospective studies in two large cohorts of European women showed that cabergoline treatment was associated with a lower incidence of postpartum breast cancer, with a meta-analysis indicating an approximate 69% reduction in risk. Our work underscores the importance of targeting postlactational involution as a strategy for the prevention of postpartum breast cancer and positions cabergoline as a novel, low-risk chemoprevention strategy.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: A subset of cutaneous melanocytic tumors has ambiguous histopathologic features that preclude reliable classification as benign or malignant. We evaluated the diagnostic yield and long-term clinical validity of expert histopathologic evaluation and, when inconclusive, additional molecular analyses in patients with ambiguous primary cutaneous melanocytic tumors. METHODS: In this prospective cohort study, consecutive patients with primary cutaneous melanocytic tumors deemed ambiguous by referring pathologists were evaluated at a tertiary dermatopathology referral center in the Netherlands from September 2018 through December 2021. Tumors underwent expert histopathologic evaluation, with next-generation sequencing, single-nucleotide polymorphism array, and targeted RNA sequencing when inconclusive. Tumors were classified as nonmelanoma, melanoma, or borderline melanoma. Clinical validity was assessed by melanoma-related events during follow-up. RESULTS: Among 258,562 patients with excised melanocytic tumors nationwide, 2,685 (1.0%) had ambiguous tumors. We included 994 patients and reached a diagnosis in 966 (97.2%): 417 (42.0%) after expert histopathologic evaluation alone and 549 (55.2%) after additional molecular analyses. Among 608 patients (61.2%) with a nonmelanoma diagnosis, no melanoma-related events occurred during median follow-up of 5.4 years (incidence, 0.0%; 95% CI, 0.0 to 0.6). Among 358 patients (36.0%) with a melanoma diagnosis, 33 of 186 (17.7%) had a positive sentinel node biopsy, and 20 developed melanoma-related events during median follow-up of 5.0 years (cumulative incidence, 5.7%; 95% CI, 3.3 to 8.1). No events occurred in 28 patients (2.8%) with a borderline melanoma diagnosis. CONCLUSION: Expert histopathologic evaluation combined with molecular analyses provided a definitive diagnosis in nearly all patients with ambiguous primary cutaneous melanocytic tumors. Long-term follow-up supported the clinical validity of this stepwise diagnostic approach.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Abusive head trauma carries higher mortality than unintentional traumatic brain injury (TBI), but whether this persists at comparable presenting severity, and how much reflects withdrawal of life-sustaining treatment (WLST), is unclear. We compared severity-matched in-hospital mortality between abusive and unintentional severe pediatric TBI and quantified the contribution of WLST. METHODS: Retrospective cohort study of the American College of Surgeons Trauma Quality Improvement Program registry (2019-2024) including children with severe TBI (Glasgow Coma Scale ≤8) from abusive or unintentional blunt mechanisms. Abusive cases were matched 1:1 to unintentional controls on 43 indicators of demographics, presenting severity, and hospital factors. Mortality was analyzed with conditional logistic regression; WLST's contribution was assessed by restriction to patients without WLST, counterfactual decomposition, and multiple imputation retaining all abusive cases. RESULTS: Crude mortality was 40.5% (abusive) vs 17.2% (unintentional). In 395 matched pairs, abusive injury was associated with higher mortality (odds ratio [OR] 1.39, 95% CI 1.01-1.90) and more frequent WLST (19.0% vs 14.2%). The association was attenuated among patients without WLST (OR 1.11, 0.71-1.71), but this underpowered finding was not reproduced after multiple imputation (1,009 pairs: mortality OR 1.58, 1.21-2.07; without WLST 1.55, 1.03-2.34). WLST mediated one-third of the excess mortality (33%, 7-60%) and preceded half of the excess deaths; the excess was confined to deaths after hospital day 1 (OR 1.65, 1.22-2.23). CONCLUSION: At comparable presenting severity, abusive TBI carries a modest excess mortality emerging after the first hospital day; roughly one-third runs through more frequent WLST and the remainder persists among children who continue treatment. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: III - retrospective comparative study (propensity-matched cohort).

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Minimally invasive (MIS) extraperitoneal ventral hernia repair (VHR) has become increasingly common, however, limited data exist comparing medium-weight (MW) versus heavyweight (HW) mesh in this setting. We hypothesized that HW mesh in this context would be associated with decreased rates of hernia recurrence at 1 year and beyond compared to MW mesh. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data from the Abdominal Core Health Quality Collaborative database, identifying adults who underwent MIS extraperitoneal (preperitoneal and/or retromuscular) VHR with either MW (40-60 g/m2) or HW (> 75 g/m2) uncoated permanent synthetic mesh from the inception of the registry to May 2025, with ≥1 year clinical or patient-reported follow-up. Propensity score matching was used to adjust for imbalances in baseline patient characteristics. The primary outcome was 1-year pragmatic hernia recurrence, defined as recurrence based on available elements of patient-reported, clinical and/or radiographic recurrence. Secondary outcomes included 30-day surgical site infection (SSI), surgical site occurrences (SSO), surgical site occurrences requiring procedural intervention (SSOPI). RESULTS: 821 patients were identified. After propensity score matching, 238 patients remained (119 MW, 119 HW). Most baseline covariates were well-matched. Patients with umbilical hernias were more likely to receive MW mesh (80% vs. 65%, p =0.009), while patients receiving HW mesh were more likely to have subxiphoid hernias (5.9% vs 15%, p =0.020). There were no documented SSI at 30 days. The rates of SSO (p =0.696), SSOPI (p =0.498), and 30-day reoperation (p =0.999) were similar between groups. At 1-year, pragmatic recurrence was similar between MW and HW patients (7.6% vs 12.6%, p =0.196). CONCLUSIONS: MW and HW mesh demonstrate comparable early and mid-term outcomes following MIS extraperitoneal VHR. Further prospective study and long-term follow-up are necessary as these techniques proliferate.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of balloon-occluded transarterial chemoembolization (B-TACE) compared with conventional (cTACE) and drug-eluting-bead transarterial chemoembolization (DEB-TACE) in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted following PRISMA guidelines and registered in PROSPERO. PubMed, Scopus, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched to 8 February 2026 for randomized and observational studies comparing B-TACE with cTACE or DEB-TACE. Tumor response (mRECIST), overall survival, and adverse events were pooled using random-effects models; risk of bias was assessed with established tools. RESULTS: Nine studies (one randomized, eight observational; 1534 patients) were included. Complete response, objective response, disease control, and progressive disease did not differ significantly between groups, with moderate-to-substantial heterogeneity. Baseline tumors were larger in the balloon-occluded group (mean difference 4.34 mm; 95% CI 1.18- 7.50; p = 0.014). Exploratory study-level analyses suggested greater relative B-TACE effects with larger tumors, particularly for complete response and disease control.Overall survival favored B-TACE in the two studies with extractable hazard ratios (HR 0.41; 95% CI 0.23 to 0.73; p = 0.002). Post-treatment liver enzymes, bilirubin, fever, and post-embolization syndrome did not differ significantly. CONCLUSION: No statistically significant differences in imaging response or safety were observed between intervention and comparator groups, while B-TACE was associated with a signal toward improved overall survival despite larger baseline tumors. Exploratory findings suggested that larger tumor size may be associated with a greater relative B-TACE effect. Given the limited evidence, these findings require confirmation in randomized controlled trials.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) are increasingly used in patients with gastrointestinal cancer (GIC). However, ICI-associated adverse event (AE) profiles in GIC remain poorly characterized, and whether AE incidence is associated with clinical outcomes is unclear. METHODS: Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) were identified through February 2025. Primary outcomes included treatment-related AEs (TRAEs) and immune-related AEs (irAEs) (any grade/Grade 3+). Single-arm random-effects meta-analysis pooled AE incidences; risk ratios (RRs) compared toxicity across ICI regimens. Digitized Kaplan-Meier curves reconstructed survival data for pooled analysis and Cox models. Weighted Spearman's tests assessed correlations between AE incidences and median overall survival (OS)/progression-free survival (PFS). RESULTS: Forty RCTs enrolling 10,233 patients investigated ICI monotherapy, dual-ICI therapy, and ICI combination regimens. Pooled any-grade TRAE incidences were 68.0% (monotherapy, 95% CI: 60%-76%, I2 = 97.4%, p < 0.001), 87.0% (dual therapy, 95% CI: 73%-100%, I2 = 98.0%, p < 0.001), and 90.0% (combination therapy, 95% CI: 83%-96%, I2 = 94.6%, p < 0.001). IrAE incidences reached 24.0% (monotherapy, 95% CI: 18%-29%, I2 = 67.2%, p < 0.05) and 37.0% (combination therapy, 95% CI: 25%-49%, I2 = 98.8%, p < 0.001). Relative to monotherapy, dual-ICI therapy elevated any-grade (RR = 1.28, 95% CI: 1.05-1.55) and grade ≥ 3 TRAEs (RR = 2.71, 95% CI: 1.84-3.99); ICI combination therapy increased any-grade (RR = 1.32, 95% CI: 1.15-1.51) and grade ≥ 3 TRAEs (RR = 2.98, 95% CI: 2.30-3.87). Any-grade TRAEs moderately correlated with median OS (R = 0.46, p < 0.001) and PFS (R = 0.50, p < 0.001). Any-grade irAEs strongly correlated with median OS (R = 0.90, p < 0.001) and moderately with PFS (R = 0.57, p < 0.001). CONCLUSION: While AE incidence is high among GIC patients receiving ICIs, most events are low-grade. Dual-ICI and ICI-based combination therapies carry higher TRAE and irAE risks than monotherapy. At the trial level, higher non-severe irAE incidence correlated with favorable survival outcomes; this exploratory ecological association does not apply to individual patients. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: This study was registered on International Platform of Registered Systematic Review and Meta-analysis Protocols (INPLASY202230144).

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Many patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) are unable to use metered dose inhaler (MDI) or dry powder inhaler effectively and require treatment with nebulized medication. No triple combination is available in nebulized form. METHODS: In this randomized, double-blind study, 314 patients with COPD received either Glycopyrronium 25 μg/Formoterol Fumarate 20 μg/Budesonide 500 μg (GB/FF/BUD Neb) by nebulization twice daily or Glycopyrronium 7.2 μg, Formoterol Fumarate 5 μg, Budesonide 160 μg MDI (GB/FF/BUD MDI) 2 Puffs twice daily for 12 weeks. The primary endpoint was change from baseline in trough forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1) at week 12. RESULTS: At week 12, GB/FF/BUD Neb was non-inferior (NI) to GB/FF/BUD MDI in change from baseline in trough FEV1 [LS mean (SE) difference -0.00 L (95% CI, -0.04 to 0.04); p < 0.001 for NI with NI margin -0.08 L). At week 12, the between group difference was 0.04 L (95% CI: -0.00 to 0.09; p = 0.070) in 2-hour post-dose FEV1 and -0.24 (95% CI: -0.42 to -0.07; p = 0.007) in the modified Medical Research Council (mMRC) dyspnoea score. There was no difference between treatments in the rescue medication use and change from baseline in trough forced vital capacity. No serious adverse event or death was reported. Overall, adverse events were comparable between the two groups. CONCLUSION: GB/FF/BUD Neb was non-inferior to GB/FF/BUD MDI in improving lung function evaluated by trough FEV1 in patients with COPD. GB/FF/BUD Neb was found to be safe and well tolerated. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: CTRI/2024/10/075606 (Clinical Trial Registry - India).

papers.abstract_en: IMPORTANCE: Despite growing interest in the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in medicine, empirical evidence on how clinicians use these tools is limited. OBJECTIVE: To characterize clinician use of an AI-enabled clinical information platform, the distribution of use across the clinical workforce, and the purpose of submitted queries. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This cross-sectional study analyzed clinicians with National Provider Identifier-verified accounts of a commonly used AI-enabled clinical information platform, OpenEvidence, from January 1, 2024, through June 30, 2026. A large language model was used to classify the clinical purpose and topic areas of a stratified random sample of 38.8 million queries. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The number of active users and clinical queries, the share of queries relative to representation in the national workforce, and the clinical purpose and topic of queries were examined. RESULTS: Overall, 952 008 clinicians (58.5% female), including 556 200 physicians, submitted 271 million queries during the 2.5-year study period. Monthly active users increased from 355 in January 2024 to 703 265 in June 2026, and average monthly queries per active user rose from 18.0 to 39.5. Nurse practitioners (44.5) and physician assistants (44.5) submitted more queries per active user-month than physicians (37.1). A higher share of queries relative to the national workforce was submitted by physicians within a decade of graduation (use ratio, 2.54) and residents and fellows (1.84). Use was also higher than average among physicians specializing in oncology and hematology (use ratio, 2.00), internal medicine (1.88), and family medicine (1.80), but lower in procedural and diagnostic specialties (ophthalmology, 0.23; radiology, 0.24; orthopedics, 0.24). Most queries addressed clinical decision-making (51.9%), particularly treatment and management (33.1%), whereas diagnosis accounted for 13.9% of queries. Queries addressing topics outside physicians' own specialties ranged from 35% among oncologists and hematologists to 88% among emergency department physicians. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Over 2.5 years, more than 950 000 US clinicians submitted greater than 270 million queries to an AI-enabled clinical information platform. Use varied across clinician types, specialties, and career stages and was frequently for treatment decisions rather than diagnostic tasks.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Financial toxicity (FT) among cancer survivors is prevalent and associated with excess morbidity and mortality. Although financial navigation (FN) has reduced FT in limited academic and urban settings, evaluation of FN within broader practice settings is needed. METHODS: We conducted a pragmatic hybrid II implementation-effectiveness clinical trial (Lessening the Impact of Financial Toxicity [LIFT]) in eight oncology practice sites, tailoring FN for four rural sites and four nonrural sites. All patients with cancer within 5 years of diagnosis, or those living with advanced disease, with a Comprehensive Score for financial Toxicity (FACIT-COST) score of ≤22 (indicating moderate-to-severe FT) who understood English were eligible. The primary effectiveness outcome was change in FACIT-COST score, pre- versus post-LIFT implementation. Patient-level secondary outcomes included the following: uptake (number served by FN/number screened positive for FT), acceptability, responsiveness, alignment with needs, patient-centeredness, and timeliness. RESULTS: Of 258 patients consented, 233 screened FT-positive, 179 received FN, 134 completed post-intervention measures, and 21 died before study completion. Participants were, on average, 53.0 years (standard deviation [SD], 13.0), mostly female (65.7%), and non-Hispanic White (56.0%) or Black (33.6%), with 9.0% identifying as Hispanic and 39.6% from a rural ZIP code. After LIFT, FACIT-COST scores significantly improved by an average 8.1 (SD, 10.0) points (P < .0001), Pre: 6.6 (SD, 5.1), Post: 14.7 (SD, 10.2), with significant increases at both rural (6.3 [SD, 9.2], P < .0001) and nonrural sites (9.3 [SD, 10.4], P < .0001). Intervention uptake was high, with nearly three quarters of those who screened positive for FT receiving FN. LIFT was broadly perceived as acceptable, responsive, aligned with patient needs, and timely. CONCLUSION: Patient-centered interventions like FN can clearly reduce FT in diverse patient populations across clinical settings and should be considered best practice.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Relapse is the dominant cause of failure after allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) for aggressive hematologic malignancies. CD45-directed radioimmunotherapy (RIT) has been investigated to intensify conditioning and augment antitumor efficacy. After gaining clinical experience with β-emitting radionuclides, attention is now shifting toward α-emitters, such as astatine-211 (211At), for their more potent and precise radiation delivery with minimized toxicity to surrounding tissues. PATIENTS AND METHODS: To our knowledge, in this first-in-human, two-stage dose-finding study, we administered a single infusion of 211At-labeled anti-CD45 monoclonal antibody before nonmyeloablative conditioning with fludarabine/2-3 Gy total body irradiation and allografting from HLA-matched or single-allele-mismatched donors in 45 adults (38-74 years of age) at a high relapse risk from myeloid malignancies or acute leukemia. RESULTS: Seventeen patients were treated in stage I with 85-591 μCi/kg of 211At. The patient receiving 591 μCi/kg developed veno-occlusive disease/sinusoidal obstruction syndrome (VOD/SOS), thereby establishing 500 μCi/kg as the protocol-defined maximum tolerated dose and prompting initiation of stage II at that dose in 28 patients. Infusion reactions were mild. 211At-CD45 RIT did not delay hematopoietic recovery, impair donor chimerism, or increase graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) rates. In stage II, six patients (all receiving sirolimus as part of GVHD prophylaxis for unrelated donor HCT) experienced VOD/SOS. Among the 13 patients with circulating blasts at baseline, blasts cleared in 12 before initiation of fludarabine/total body irradiation, demonstrating immediate cytotoxic activity. Estimated 1-year relapse-free and overall survival were 42% (95% CI, 28%-56%) and 49% (34%-62%), respectively. CONCLUSION: 211At-CD45 RIT can be incorporated into nonmyeloablative conditioning, with liver toxicity defining activity limits. Evidence of antitumor efficacy supports phase II evaluation.

papers.abstract_en: Coral reefs are diverse marine ecosystems that provide ecological functions and economic and social benefits across over 100 tropical countries. Warming driven by climate change is a primary threat to coral reefs and is increasing the frequency of global coral bleaching events. Here we reassessed the IUCN Red List status of 892 reef-building coral species, first assessed in 2008 1. Because species-level population trends are unavailable for most reef-building corals, population reductions were inferred using proxies based on global coral cover trends and projected annual severe bleaching under SSP2-4.5, both over three decades, adjusted using trait-based estimates of species vulnerability. Of the 774 species with sufficient data to be assessed, 340 (44%) were classified as threatened under IUCN Red List criteria. Thirty-three species were assessed as Critically Endangered, 251 as Endangered, and 56 as Vulnerable, most due to risk of population reduction associated with projected thermal stress. These findings predate the three hottest years on record and the fourth global coral bleaching event (2023-2025), and the first exceedance for an annual mean of the 1.5oC global warming threshold. The findings reinforce the importance of limiting further warming to maintain coral biodiversity and reef ecosystem function. The Red List assesses the relative extinction risk of species, whereby species are placed in categories of increasing risk by comparing their population size, decline and geographic range against standardised thresholds. The Red List does not predict whether or when a species may go extinct. As the ranges of coral species remain under-surveyed, future assessments would be strengthened by species-level population data and thermal-stress and recovery metrics that better capture range-representative dynamics.

papers.abstract_en: D2C7-ATC is a recombinant antibody-toxin conjugate (ATC) targeting wild-type epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) and mutant EGFR variant III (EGFRvIII). We conducted a single-arm, single-site, open-label phase 1 trial evaluating a single infusion of D2C7-ATC via convection-enhanced delivery in the enhancing disease of 81 patients with biopsy-confirmed recurrent malignant glioma. The primary objective was to determine toxicity and the recommended phase 2 dose (RP2D) of D2C7-ATC. Secondary objectives included describing overall survival (OS) and assessing the association between EGFR expression and OS. The median overall survival (mOS) was 7.9 months among 72 patients with isocitrate dehydrogenase wild-type recurrent glioblastoma (IDHwt rGBM), including 35 patients in the dose-escalation stage (40 to 35,032 ng ml-1) and 37 patients in the dose-expansion stage (RP2D of 6,920 ng ml-1). D2C7-ATC was generally well tolerated, with mainly grade 1-2 treatment-related adverse events (67%). The maximum tolerated dose was exceeded at 35,032 ng ml-1, where four patients experienced dose-limiting toxicities, including grade 4 (N = 2) and grade 3 (N = 2) events. Eight patients died on trial; all deaths were unrelated to D2C7-ATC. Univariate analyses identified survival-associated biomarkers, including tumor D2C7 antibody reactivity, circulating cytokines, a tumor inflammatory gene signature and neutrophils, monocytes and lymphocytes in blood. Notably, patients with IDHwt rGBM with a D2C7 antibody reactivity score of <1.5+ in pre-treatment tumor had an mOS of 17.38 months, whereas those with low IL-8 in post-treatment plasma had an mOS of 16.6 months. These findings indicate that EGFR-targeted D2C7-ATC therapy prolongs survival in a subset of patients with IDHwt rGBM via intratumoral and systemic immune activation. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) has been shown to be beneficial in persons with type 1 diabetes and others with insulin-treated type 2 diabetes, but its role in the treatment of persons with type 2 diabetes not being treated with insulin has needed further study. METHODS: In a 26-week trial conducted at 22 primary care practices in the United States, we randomly assigned adults with type 2 diabetes who were not using insulin to either CGM or routine care (control). The primary outcome was the glycated hemoglobin level at 26 weeks. Key CGM-measured secondary outcomes were tested hierarchically to control the type I error rate. RESULTS: A total of 145 participants were assigned to the CGM group, and 138 to the routine-care group. Participants ranged in age from 21 to 84 years. The mean (±SD) glycated hemoglobin level decreased from 8.8±1.3% at baseline to 7.2±1.1% at 26 weeks in the CGM group and from 8.7±1.2% to 8.0±1.4% in the routine-care group (adjusted mean difference, -0.9 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -1.1 to -0.6; P<0.001). The mean percentage of time that the CGM-measured glucose level was in the glucose-level range of 70 to 180 mg per deciliter was 21 percentage points higher (95% CI, 16 to 26) with CGM than with routine care (P<0.001). The between-group difference in the percentage of time that the glucose level was below 54 mg per deciliter was -0.17 percentage points (95% CI, -0.27 to -0.11; P<0.001 for noninferiority); the difference in the percentage of time that the glucose level was below 70 mg per deciliter was -0.20 percentage points (95% CI, -0.43 to -0.09; P<0.001 for noninferiority; P = 0.004 for superiority). No severe hypoglycemia events were reported. CONCLUSIONS: Among adults with type 2 diabetes that was not being treated with insulin and was being managed in a primary care setting, the use of CGM led to a greater reduction in the glycated hemoglobin level and to a lower risk of hyperglycemia than routine care. papers.abstract_en: Chitosan, a major fungal cell wall component, activates plant immunity, yet the underlying perception mechanism remains unknown. In this study, we identified OsFID1, an apoplast-localized DUF26 domain protein, as a chitosan-binding receptor essential for chitosan-triggered immunity. OsFID1 forms a receptor complex with OsFID2, a plasma membrane-localized DUF26 receptor-like kinase, to mediate chitosan sensing and immune activation, requiring OsFID2 phosphorylation for function. The OsFID1-OsFID2 complex confers broad-spectrum resistance to fungal pathogens. OsFID1 homologs are conserved in land plants, which show chitosan-binding activity in both monocots and dicots. Ectopic expression of OsFID1 in wheat and maize enhanced fungal resistance without growth penalty. These findings uncover a conserved receptor complex for direct chitosan sensing, advancing our understanding of plant-fungus interactions and providing a potential strategy for engineering durable fungal resistance crops.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Phospholipid metabolism (PLM) has been implicated in macrophage polarization and tumor progression in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). Metabolic intermediates such as lysophosphatidylcholine modulate macrophage surface receptor signaling, while inhibition of phospholipid synthesis may attenuate tumor-associated macrophage (TAM) infiltration and suppress LUAD progression. However, macrophage-centered PLM-related prognostic signatures in LUAD remain incompletely characterized. METHODS: We performed an integrative multi-omics analysis combining single-cell RNA sequencing, bulk transcriptomic profiling, and clinical data from TCGA and GEO cohorts. Macrophage-related genes (MacRGs) were identified using single-cell analysis and high-dimensional weighted gene co-expression network analysis (hdWGCNA). Phospholipid metabolism-related module genes were determined through differential expression analysis and WGCNA. Candidate genes were prioritized using machine learning and Cox regression analyses, followed by construction and external validation of a multigene risk model. Functional enrichment, immune microenvironment profiling, mutation landscape analysis, estimated drug sensitivity, and pseudotime trajectory analyses were performed to explore the biological relevance of the signature. Experimental validation was conducted using LUAD tissues and cell models. RESULTS: A four-gene macrophage-PLM-related signature was constructed to calculate a risk score that stratified patients into high- and low-risk groups with significantly different overall survival. The risk score and T stage were independent prognostic factors, and an integrated nomogram showed acceptable prognostic performance. Functional analyses revealed distinct metabolic and signaling pathway enrichment patterns between risk groups, with 40 shared pathways across the four hub genes. The high-risk group exhibited an altered immune microenvironment characterized by differential infiltration of 20 immune cell subsets, immune checkpoint expression changes, lower ESTIMATE scores, and distinct TIDE profiles. Somatic mutation patterns and tumor mutational burden differed between groups. Drug-sensitivity estimation identified 105 compounds with differential estimated IC50 values between risk groups. DPYSL2 expression was associated with macrophage polarization dynamics, and DPYSL2 overexpression suppressed LUAD cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and clonogenicity in vitro. CONCLUSION: We identified a macrophage-phospholipid metabolism-associated four-gene prognostic signature that provides prognostic information and reflects immune-metabolic remodeling in LUAD. These findings support further investigation of macrophage-phospholipid metabolism-related genes as candidate biomarkers and may inform future therapeutic stratification studies in LUAD.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Thrombocytopenia during immune checkpoint inhibitor treatment in lung cancer may be coded as immune, marrow suppression, coagulation, or non-specific. We tested whether coding-defined report phenotypes differed across co-reported treatment contexts. METHODS: We analyzed FAERS (2015Q1-2026Q2) and JADER through Japanese fiscal 2025Q4 (31 March 2026). Strict primary lung cancer reports were grouped as ICI without chemotherapy (C1), ICI plus chemotherapy (C2), or chemotherapy without ICI (C3). Firth models compared mutually exclusive immune-like and marrow-like anchors. Complementary analyses evaluated the broad cohort, treatment date compatibility, C3 small-cell influence, phenotype variants, onset windows, treatment-variable ablation in elastic-net report phenotype models, and a 120-report random stratified blinded review with independent ratings, third-person adjudication, inverse-selection weighting, and bootstrap uncertainty. RESULTS: FAERS included 1,362 immune-like or marrow-like anchors. Relative to C1, adjusted odds ratios (ORs) for immune-like versus marrow-like phenotype were 0.111 (95% CI, 0.069-0.173) in C2 and 0.014 (0.006-0.029) in C3; C3 was exploratory because only eight reports were immune-like. In 2,835 broad cohort reports, adjusted immune-like composition was 13.0% (95% bootstrap interval, 11.0%-15.1%) in C1 and 4.7% (3.4%-6.2%) in C2. Treatment date and stricter phenotype analyses were directionally consistent. JADER reproduced the C2 versus C1 direction but showed calibration shift; treatment-variable ablation reduced cross-database discrimination. Reviewers agreed on 111/120 reports (92.5%; 95% CI, 87.5%-96.7%; Cohen's κ, 0.897; Gwet's AC1, 0.901). In the locked 927-report frame, design-weighted final categories were 23.4% immune probable, 37.3% immune possible, 13.6% indeterminate, and 25.8% non-immune probable. Among 100 determinate reports, weighted AUROC was 0.892 (0.827-0.948), PR-AUC 0.956 (0.922-0.982), and calibration-in-the-large intercept 2.054 (1.707-2.432), indicating underprediction. CONCLUSION: Coding-defined thrombocytopenia report composition differed across treatment contexts. Blinded review supported reproducible structured category assignment and score-based report ordering, while calibration shift and treatment-variable ablation defined important limits. Findings support pharmacovigilance case prioritization and hypothesis generation, not clinical diagnosis, incidence estimation, patient-level etiologic attribution, or causal inference.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Acute exacerbation (AE) is the most lethal event of idiopathic inflammatory myopathy-associated interstitial lung disease (IIM-ILD). This exploratory study compared clinical, radiomics, and combined predictor strategies across five survival-learning algorithms for survival risk stratification. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 78 patients with AE-IIM-ILD and divided them into a training cohort (n = 54; 20 deaths) and a held-out internal testing cohort (n = 24; 9 deaths), stratified by observed mortality event status. Three predictor strategies were evaluated: a clinical strategy comprising PaO2/FiO2 ratio, neutrophil percentage (NEU%), and arthritis-related symptoms; a radiomics strategy comprising two selected radiomics features; and a combined strategy comprising PaO2/FiO2 ratio, arthritis-related symptoms, and a composite radiomics score (Rad-score). Each strategy was evaluated using five survival-learning algorithms. Harrell's concordance index (C-index) was the primary discrimination metric, with mean time-dependent area under the curve (AUC) used as a secondary measure. RESULTS: During the 1-year follow-up, 29 deaths were observed. Performance rankings varied across predictor strategies, algorithms, and evaluation metrics. The combined-Random Survival Forest configuration demonstrated the highest training-cohort C-index among the 15 configurations. Its mean time-dependent AUC was 0.923 (95% CI: 0.860-0.970) in the training cohort and 0.915 (95% CI: 0.736-0.986) in the testing cohort, with corresponding C-indices of 0.874 (95% CI: 0.803-0.940) and 0.842 (95% CI: 0.673-0.971), respectively. The model stratified patients into high- and low-risk groups with distinct observed survival trajectories. CONCLUSION: In this exploratory cohort, integrating selected clinical variables with a quantitative CT Rad-score using RSF showed promising numerical discrimination and risk-stratification performance. These findings suggest that clinical and quantitative imaging information may provide complementary prognostic information after AE-IIM-ILD.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Immunogenic cell death (ICD) and tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) are biologically distinct yet interconnected components of antitumor immunity. ICD promotes danger-associated immune activation, whereas TLSs organize local adaptive immune responses. However, how these processes jointly affect immune heterogeneity, prognosis, and therapeutic responsiveness in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains unclear. METHODS: To define the coordinated roles of TLS- and ICD-related programs in LUAD, we used a multi-cohort and multi-layer analytical framework. This framework included transcriptomic analysis, Mendelian randomization, consensus machine-learning prognostic modeling, immune landscape characterization, single-cell RNA sequencing, multiplex immunohistochemistry, immunotherapy response assessment, exploratory drug screening, structural analyses, and multilayer network topology analysis. RESULTS: TLS- and ICD-associated genes were transcriptionally dysregulated in LUAD. By integrating 13 machine-learning algorithms, we developed 801 candidate prognostic models and identified optimal TLS- and ICD-related models that stratified patients effectively into high- and low-risk groups. These models showed strong performance in TCGA and remained robust across six external cohorts. Low-risk tumors had higher TLS+ICD scores than high-risk tumors. Immune landscape analysis indicated that low-risk tumors had elevated immune scores, enhanced antigen presentation, cytotoxic T/NK-cell signatures, checkpoint activation, and lower Tumor Immune Dysfunction and Exclusion (TIDE) scores, suggesting a more immunotherapy-responsive microenvironment. Consistently, higher TLS+ICD scores correlated with improved survival and greater immunotherapy responsiveness in independent cohorts. Mendelian randomization and survival analyses prioritized CD40, CD5, and GFI1 as candidate TLS-ICD immune-regulatory genes, with single-cell and mIHC analyses defining their major cellular origins, spatial protein phenotypes, and prognostic relevance. Drug prediction, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations identified CAY10576, SCH772984, and SZ4TA2 as potential therapeutic agents for high-risk LUAD. Multilayer gene regulatory network reconstruction and GLMY homology analysis revealed progressive disruption of higher-order immune-regulatory organization from normal to tumor tissues and between low TLS-risk/low ICD-risk (LL-risk) and high TLS-risk/high ICD-risk (HH-risk) states. CONCLUSIONS: TLS- and ICD-related programs jointly delineate clinically significant immune states in LUAD through convergent transcriptomic, genetic, single-cell, spatial, pharmacological, and systems-level evidence, and are associated with immune microenvironment remodeling, immunotherapy responsiveness, prognosis, and therapeutic vulnerability. These findings establish a biomarker-guided, machine learning-supported framework for LUAD risk stratification and may inform more precise immunotherapy-oriented therapeutic strategies.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Pediatric patients who experience firearm injury may be at risk for subsequent reinjury, yet the timing and predictors of recurrence remain poorly defined. Characterizing reinjury patterns at both individual and system levels is essential for informing targeted prevention strategies. METHODS: We performed a retrospective review (2010-2024) of patients aged 0-18 years presenting with non-self-inflicted firearm injuries to two Level I pediatric and adult trauma centers. Cross-institutional database linkage was used to identify reinjury events. Cumulative incidence functions estimated reinjury risk over time, accounting for death as a competing risk. Univariate and multivariate Cox proportional hazards models evaluated independent predictors of reinjury. RESULTS: Among 834 patients (84.9% male, 79% Black; median age 17 years [IQR 15-18]), 67 died from their index injury and 75 sustained a subsequent firearm injury at a median of 22 months (IQR 12-61). No reinjury events occurred among children younger than 11 years. Cumulative reinjury incidence at one, three, and five years was 2.5% (1.4-3.6), 5.9% (4.2-7.5), and 7.8% (5.8-9.7), respectively. Assault-related index injury (aHR 2.18, 95% CI 1.10-4.35), lower injury severity (aHR 0.59, 95% CI 0.36-0.97), and treatment at an adult trauma center (aHR 3.43, 95% CI 1.46-8.06) were independently associated with increased reinjury risk. CONCLUSIONS: Firearm reinjury among pediatric patients is concentrated in adolescence and often occurs years after the initial event. Reinjured youth were more likely to have been assaulted, uninsured, and initially treated for relatively minor injuries-factors that may limit engagement with supportive services. These findings underscore the need for developmentally tailored violence-prevention and resource-linkage interventions initiated at the time of first injury.
