papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Absence of reliable risk assessment and monitoring of fetal wellbeing during labour remains a major clinical challenge worldwide. Cardiotocography (CTG) is commonly used to monitor the fetal heart rate, but its misinterpretation or delays in clinical escalation contribute to poor birth outcomes. We aimed to develop a novel prognostic model for the prediction of severe fetal compromise at birth, combining known clinical risk factors with the first 20 min of CTG monitoring. METHODS: In this retrospective, model development and validation study, we used routinely collected, fully anonymised maternity data from three databases: the John Radcliffe Hospital (Oxford, UK; 1993-2024; model training and testing), the Rosie Hospital (Cambridge, UK; 2016-22; external validation), and the Stockholm-Gotland region (Sweden; 2018-20; independent external validation). Oxford and Cambridge datasets were accessed from maternity and neonatal unit electronic health records; Stockholm-Gotland data were accessed as part of the larger Stockholm-Gotland Perinatal Cohort. Singleton births at 36 weeks and 0 days of gestation or more undergoing intrapartum CTG monitoring, whether labour was spontaneous or induced, were included. Clinical risk factors used for model development were maternal age, gestational age, nulliparity, pre-eclampsia, diabetes in pregnancy, thick meconium, and maximal recorded maternal temperature in labour. Quantitative CTG features included in the model were fetal heart rate baseline, short-term variability, decelerative capacity, number of accelerations, and number of prolonged decelerations, and were extracted using the Oxford intrapartum computer-based algorithms. Birth outcomes were defined in three mutually exclusive groups: severe compromise, intermediate compromise, and healthy. Fit4Labour risk score (ie, estimated probability of severe compromise) was stratified into four risk groups: >95th centile of Fit4Labour risk score, >85th and ≤95th centile of Fit4Labour risk score, >25th and ≤85th centile of Fit4Labour risk score, and ≤25th centile of Fit4Labour risk score. Model accuracy was assessed by use of partial receiver operating characteristic curves and comparison with a clinical benchmark (sensitivity at 15% screen-positive rate). FINDINGS: 147 350 births with at least 20 min of CTG data were analysed: 91 378 from Oxford 1993-2024 (73 443 for training and testing [Oxford 1993-2019] and 17 935 for internal validation [Oxford 2020-24]), 14 709 from Cambridge 2016-22 (external validation), and 41 263 from Stockholm-Gotland 2018-20 (independent external validation). The rate of severe compromise was higher in the highest-risk group (>95th centile) than in the lowest-risk group (≤25th centile) across all validation datasets: 0·9% (95% CI 0·28-1·51) in the highest risk group versus 0·1% (0·01-0·21) in the lowest-risk group in the Oxford 2020-24 dataset; 0·3% (0·00-0·65) versus 0·1% (0·00-0·22) in the Cambridge 2016-22 dataset; and 0·9% (0·47-1·27) versus 0·2% (0·08-0·23) in the Stockholm-Gotland 2018-20 dataset. At a fixed screen-positive rate of 15%, 20-min Fit4Labour had a sensitivity of 33·4% (95% CI 28·31-38·56), compared with the clinical benchmark sensitivity of 39·9% (95% CI 32·59-47·18, p=0·18), and showed consistent performance across all validation datasets. INTERPRETATION: Fit4Labour is a robust prognostic model, readily applicable around labour onset and extensively validated with retrospective data from sites with different maternity demographics and clinical care practices. Fit4Labour relies on routinely available data and could produce interpretable output in real time, providing timely individualised risk stratification that is data-driven, objective, and reproducible. papers.abstract_en: Lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) lacks effective targeted therapies despite frequent hyperactivation of the PI3K/AKT pathway, and the contribution of adaptor proteins to this process remains poorly defined. Here, we identify Insulin Receptor Substrate 4 (IRS4) as a common substrate of Src kinase and the phosphatase RPTPα, and uncover a previously unrecognized, conserved phosphorylation site at YY111/112 within the IRS4 PH domain. Src-mediated phosphorylation at this site is essential for IRS4-driven proliferation, anchorage-independent growth, and invasiveness in LUSC cells. Mechanistically, phosphorylation at YY111/112 induces conformational rearrangements in IRS4 that enhance the recruitment of the p85β SH2 domain to the YXXM motif of IRS4, thereby promoting AKT activation without altering IRS4 protein stability or subcellular distribution. An IRS4-derived cell-permeable phosphopeptide containing pYY111/112 disrupts the Src-IRS4 interaction and significantly suppresses tumor growth in vivo in a YY111/112-dependent manner. Consistently, YY111/112 phosphorylation is markedly elevated in human LUSC tissues and correlates with advanced disease stages. Collectively, these findings define a Src-IRS4-PI3K/AKT signaling axis and identify YY111/112 as a critical regulatory site of IRS4 and a potential therapeutic vulnerability in LUSC.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Peristomal bulging and external stoma prolapse are the most common long-term complications following stoma formation. This systematic review aims to describe available evidence on the incidence of parastomal hernia, subcutaneous prolapse and external stomal prolapse following open versus minimally invasive intestinal resections with definitive stoma formation. METHODS: In this systematic review and meta-analysis, a literature search was performed to include studies published in the last 15 years on intestinal resections with a definitive ileostomy or colostomy formation and a follow-up of more than 12 months, reporting on PSH and/or subcutaneous prolapse and/or external stoma prolapse after laparoscopic or robotic, and open surgery. The incidence of PSH after open versus minimally invasive surgery was the primary outcome, and secondary outcomes included other stoma-related complications such as subcutaneous stoma prolapse and external stoma prolapse, and outcomes. RESULTS: In total six studies (one randomised controlled trial and five observational studies) on 1480 patients with a definitive stoma were included (731 open, 749 laparoscopic). All studies reported PSH as an outcome, no study reported the incidence of subcutaneous prolapse and one study reported on external stoma prolapse. There was consistent trend toward higher PSH rates following laparoscopic resections, both in clinically (RR 1.89 (95% CI 1.39-2.58)) and radiologically (RR 1.70 (95% CI 0.89-3.28)) assessed hernias. CONCLUSIONS: Minimally invasive intestinal resection may be associated with a higher incidence of PSH than open surgery, but the certainty of the evidence is very low. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Patient values influence preference-sensitive decisions in benign foregut (upper gastrointestinal) surgery, but their incorporation into guideline development is unclear. This systematic review evaluated how patient perspectives are included in clinical practice guidelines (CPGs) and whether involvement is associated with quality. METHODS: Databases and society websites were searched for CPGs addressing endoscopic or surgical management of benign foregut disease from January 2010 to March 2026. Two reviewers screened records, extracted data, mapped involvement across the 10-stage Armstrong framework, and assessed quality using AGREE II. RESULTS: Twenty-six CPGs were included. All used evidence-grading methods, but only 8 (31%) reported direct patient involvement. Six additional CPGs (23%) considered patient values indirectly through literature review and clinician assumptions. No CPG published before 2018 reported direct involvement. Among patient-involved CPGs, engagement most often occurred during recommendation development (8/8), evidence interpretation (5/8), and question or outcome formulation (5/8). None reported patient involvement in dissemination, implementation, updating, or evaluation of engagement. Later publication year was associated with direct involvement (OR 1.54 per year). In unadjusted analyses patient-involved CPGs had higher AGREE II scores for clarity, applicability, and editorial independence, but this did not remain statistically significant in sensitivity analyses restricting publication year and methodologist involvement. CONCLUSIONS: Direct patient involvement remains uncommon and concentrated in recommendation development rather than the entirety of guideline development. Foregut-related surgical societies should combine patient-preference evidence with transparently reported patient partnership from priority setting through implementation and updating.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: North American data regarding long-term efficacy and durability of endoscopic sleeve gastroplasty (ESG) are remarkably scarce outside of clinical trial settings hampering our understanding of its optimal role in the obesity care continuum. The aims of this study are to compare safety and efficacy of elective ESG versus laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy (LSG) at 6 months using accredited MBSAQIP centers. METHODS: Data were obtained from the Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery Accreditation and Quality Improvement Program (MBSAQIP) database for 2023 and merged with the 6‑month follow‑up data file. The primary objectives of the study were to characterize the long-term six-month changes in weight and metabolic comorbidities of ESG patients in contrast to their LSG counterparts. Logistic regression models were to evaluate for differences in six-month serious complications and emergency department readmissions between ESG and LSG. RESULTS: A total of 115,476 patients were included, comprising 114,967 LSG and 509 ESG procedures. Patients undergoing ESG were slightly older (44.5 ± 11.2 vs. 42.4 ± 11.9 years, p = 0.0001) and had lower baseline BMI (40.9 ± 8.6 vs. 45.0 ± 7.8 kg/m2, p < 0.0001) and mean body weight (113.2 ± 28 vs. 124.5 ± 26.3 kg). At 6 months, LSG resulted in greater weight reduction, with larger BMI loss (8.2 ± 10.8 vs. 3.9 ± 12.0 kg/m2, p < 0.0001), and total weight loss (22.6 ± 35.6 vs. 11.1 ± 37.7 kg, p < 0.0001). For patients undergoing LSG, there was a near 50% reduction in medication/insulin-dependent diabetes along with improvements in rates of dyslipidemia, hypertension, and sleep apnea. Importantly, no clinically meaningful comorbidity improvements from baseline to 6 months were seen following ESG. CONCLUSION: When compared to ESG at 6 months, LSG provides an improvement in total body weight loss, has a reduced operative time, and is associated with dramatic metabolic comorbidity improvement including a reduction in resolution of medication and insulin-dependent diabetes. No clinically meaningful comorbidity resolution was seen in patients receiving ESG compared to LSG at 6 months although this cohort was less comorbid at baseline.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Implementation of artificial intelligence (AI) in surgery may revolutionize assessment of operative techniques through video capture, auto-segmentation and auto-analysis. The aim of this study was to utilize recordings of a highly standardized surgical intervention, testing the ability of commercially available AI software to auto-segment operative footage in a clinically meaningful way. METHODS: Twenty-five critical steps in liver graft back-table preparations for connection to a commercially available normothermic perfusion liver pump were determined. Five operative videos were captured manually edited. In addition, using the AI-based GoPro auto-edit feature, the last two recordings were auto-segmented for separate analysis and comparison against the manually edited footage. Each manual and auto-segmented video was assessed for: a) inclusion of each one of the 25 steps, (b) technical performance and completion. The assessment was conducted by an independent experienced transplant surgeon using a modified Likert scale (0-not captured, 1-poor, 2-average, 3-excellent). RESULTS: Reviewing and rating AI auto-segmented videos was 16 times faster compared to raw video review. Reviewing and rating AI auto-segmented videos was 96 times faster compared to manually segmented recordings, accounting for time needed to edit raw videos. The average number of steps captured between both raw videos and the manually edited videos was 22.5. The average number of steps captured across the AI auto-segmented videos was 19.5 (87%). The average technical grade for the raw and the manually edited videos was 2.58 ± 0.71, and 2.14 ± 0.99 for the AI auto-segmented videos, denoting a rating congruency of 82.9%. CONCLUSION: AI-based auto-segmentation is an attractive tool for assessment of surgical performance, as it significantly expedites the editing process to prepare footage for review by subject matter experts. To which extent this approach will be applicable outside highly standardized surgical interventions must be further studied.

papers.abstract_en: Glycans play fundamental roles in T cell biology; however, the glycome landscape of γδ T cells remains to be unlocked. Despite the growing importance of γδ T cells in host defense, tissue homeostasis, and diseases, the glycosylation mechanisms guiding their activation, commitment, and function remain poorly defined. By performing single-cell RNA sequencing, we revealed that type 3/γδ T17/interleukin-17A (IL-17A)-committed γδ T cells rely on (N-acetylglucosaminyltransferase 1) MGAT1-MGAT5-mediated branched N-glycosylation. We further demonstrated that the absence of branched N-glycans on γδ T cells acts as a peripheral signal, driving an IL-17A-pro-inflammatory phenotype, alongside a shift to a Vγ4+ subset and the imprinting of innate-like properties. This altered glycoform of type 3 γδ T cells was shown to induce severe psoriasis. γδ T cells from patients with autoimmune and inflammatory diseases exhibited a deficiency in branched N-glycans. Glycan supplementation can reprogram γδ T cells toward a less-pathogenic state, highlighting N-glycans as a previously unrecognized immune checkpoint for γδ T cells.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: Osteoarthritis (OA) involves the structural failure of the joint unit, where the subchondral bone plate and associated vascular niche serve as a critical barrier and mechanical support for articular cartilage. This study investigates R-spondin 2 (Rspo2) as a mediator of instability within the subchondral bone plate-associated vascular niche and evaluates whether its pharmacological neutralization attenuates niche disruption and preserves osteochondral integrity. METHOD: Human tibial-plateau subchondral bone scRNA-seq (GSE196678) and clinical specimens were analyzed to identify Wnt-related pathways. OA was induced in mice via ACLT+DMM surgery. Weekly intra-articular administration of recombinant Rspo2, an Rspo2-neutralizing antibody (Rspo2-NAb), or the Wnt inhibitor DKK1 began on postoperative day 3. Subchondral bone remodeling and cartilage degeneration were assessed in separate groups of mice at postoperative days 30 and 60. RESULTS: The scRNA-seq analysis identified Wnt-related expression patterns in OA subchondral endothelial cells (ECs). Histology showed a higher percentage of CD31+/p-β-catenin (Ser675)+ cells in OA specimens than in controls. In vitro, rhRspo2 enhanced endothelial proliferation and tube formation, whereas conditioned medium from Rspo2-overexpressing ECs promoted osteogenic and osteoclastic differentiation and disrupted chondrocyte homeostasis; these effects were attenuated by Rspo2-NAb or DKK1, consistent with involvement of Wnt/β-catenin signaling. Early postoperative administration of Rspo2-NAb or DKK1 reduced subchondral bone plate remodeling and the proportion of CD31+EMCN+ cells, and attenuated cartilage degeneration in vivo. CONCLUSIONS: These findings support a paracrine role for endothelial-derived Rspo2 in vitro and the potential of early Rspo2 neutralization to attenuate bone remodeling and cartilage degeneration in experimental OA.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Placental foetal vascular malperfusion (PFVM) is a chronic disorder characterised by impaired blood flow and abnormal vascular development, inducing adverse neonatal outcomes. Long chain polyunsaturated fatty acids (LC-PUFAs) play a crucial role in placenta health. We aimed to explore the role of genetic variation in LC-PUFA metabolism in PFVM risk as well as underlying mechanisms. METHODS: Associations were examined between two functional polymorphisms (rs174538 and rs174556) of the fatty acid desaturase 1 (FADS1) gene encoding the rate-limiting enzyme for LC-PUFA metabolism and PFVM among pregnant women (n = 646). Placental transcriptomes were correlated with PFVM and FADS1 genotypes. Various assays were performed in human umbilical vein endothelial cells and trophoblasts with FADS1 inhibitor and LC-PUFA interventions to characterise their function changes. FINDINGS: Low-function alleles of both polymorphisms were significantly associated with increased PFVM risk and decreased placental FADS1 transcription level. In placenta tissue, lower FADS1 expression is also associated with PFVM. PFVM-associated genes are enriched to pathways related to immune responses, apoptosis, and angiogenesis, which overlap with the genes and pathways associated with the risk alleles and demonstrate a cell-type enrichment to endothelial cells. In vitro, FADS1 inhibition impairs multiple functions of and interactions between endothelial and trophoblast cells. These impairments are reversed by LC-PUFA supplementation. INTERPRETATION: These findings highlight the impact of maternal LC-PUFA homoeostasis in placenta health and suggest that maternal FADS1 variants can potentially be an early diagnostic marker for PFVM. Our data supports PUFA metabolism as a precision therapeutic or preventive target to reduce placental dysfunction risk. FUNDING: NIH, Wayne State University and Michigan State University.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Adverse drug events (ADEs) are a critical indicator of patient safety but are often documented only in free-text clinical notes. The potential of recent advances in natural language processing (NLP), particularly generative large language models (LLMs), to identify ADEs remains understudied. This study aimed to compare the performance of multiple LLMs in identifying ADE-Drug relationships in inpatient and ambulatory clinical notes. METHODS: We used clinical notes from the 2018 National NLP Clinical Challenge (n2c2) ADE dataset (inpatient; n = 505) and from outpatient encounters (n = 2555) between October 1, 2018, and December 31, 2019, at a large academic medical center based in New England. Notes were pre-processed into snippets for model input. Evaluated Models included: GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Llama 3.2-3B and their instruction fine-tuned variants (including low-rank adapters for Llama). Performance was assessed using both strict and relaxed evaluations (precision, recall, and F1) for all models, followed by manual evaluation (exact semantic match, partial match, missing ADE, drug mention only, not a drug, or wrong) of the two best-performing models. FINDINGS: Of the 1048 notes in the local test split, 450 (42.9%) contained at least one ADE. The n2c2 test set included 202 notes, of which 155 (76.7%) contained at least one ADE. GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini were the top-performing models among those evaluated. GPT-4o consistently outperformed GPT-4o-mini in ADE extraction across both datasets, with higher F1-scores (0.524 vs. 0.381) and a more balanced precision-recall profile. Both models captured ADEs effectively in explicit and complex clinical contexts, although limitations included misclassification of pre-existing allergies and occasional conflation of therapeutic indications with adverse effects. GPT-4o achieved higher exact match coverage and fewer errors across clinical notes, indicating more reliable performance in both inpatient and ambulatory settings. INTERPRETATION: This work establishes a foundation for integrating LLM methods into real-world drug safety surveillance, with direct implications for improving patient safety. FUNDING: None.

papers.abstract_en: Missed genetic deletions can prevent cancer patients from receiving effective targeted therapy. Standard pipelines, such as TSO500, use bin count averaging for copy number variation detection but often overlook focal events. To address this, we developed a machine learning (ML) pipeline for deletion detection and zygosity evaluation within the MASTERsg precision oncology program. We focused on the tumor suppressor gene PTEN, whose loss confers sensitivity to mTOR/Akt inhibition. An Extreme Gradient Boosting model trained on PTEN-deleted and wild-type tumor samples identified focal deletions missed by the TSO500 pipeline and CNVkit that were associated with concordant PTEN protein loss by immunohistochemistry. Importantly, the model detected PTEN deletions in 33/204 profiled samples that were classified as PTEN wild-type by TSO500; 75% (15/20) of stainable cases showed absent or reduced PTEN protein expression. These findings demonstrate the potential of ML to enhance panel sequencing, uncovering therapeutically relevant alterations missed by established diagnostic methods.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Cancer remains a serious public health challenge in the United States. Six major cancers (female breast, colorectal, liver, lung/bronchus, pancreas, and prostate) account for a substantial proportion of the national cancer burden. Understanding the changes in the incidence of these cancers over time can provide insights for prevention and control. This study examined temporal trends in the cancer incidence according to age at onset and stage at diagnosis. METHODS: This population-based study analyzed data from the United States Cancer Statistics database for 2001-2023, including all 50 states and the District of Columbia. Joinpoint regression was used to estimate annual percent changes (APCs) and average annual percent changes (AAPCs), with corresponding 95% confidence intervals (CIs), based on age-adjusted incidence rates per 100,000 people. Of note, incidence rates from 2020 data were excluded from the Joinpoint models because COVID-19 pandemic disruptions affected cancer screening, diagnosis, and reporting. RESULTS: From 2001 to 2023, the incidence of lung and colorectal cancers declined, particularly among older adults (aged ≥50 years) (lung cancer: AAPC -2.09; 95% CI: -2.27, -1.90; colorectal cancer AAPC -2.70; 95% CI: -2.83, -2.56). In contrast, the incidence of colorectal, pancreatic, and breast cancers increased among younger adults (aged <50 years), whereas the incidence of liver and lung cancer declined. Moreover, prostate cancer incidence declined over time despite modest rebound in recent years (AAPC 1.83; 95% CI: 0.53, 3.14). Stage-specific analyses revealed increasing rates of early-stage diagnoses for several cancers, while late-stage cancer incidence increased for pancreatic and colorectal cancers (especially among younger adults). CONCLUSIONS: Cancer incidence varied substantially by cancer type, age, and stage at diagnosis. The rising incidence of colorectal, pancreatic, and breast cancers among younger adults underscores the need for continued research into risk factors, early detection, and prevention strategies.

papers.abstract_en: The gut microbiota is well established as a key modulator of systemic immunity, with growing evidence supporting its impact on lung cancer immunotherapy outcomes. However, the contributions of the lung microbiota and the recently recognized intratumoral microbiota remain less defined. This review synthesizes current evidence on the gut-lung axis, consolidating the tripartite regulatory network of gut, lung, and intratumoral microbiota in shaping the lung cancer immune microenvironment and immunotherapy response. We discuss how gut-derived metabolites such as indole-3-propionic acid may remotely modulate CD8+ T cell stemness, how lung microbiota locally influence alveolar macrophage polarization through pattern recognition receptor signaling, and how intratumoral microbiota have been implicated in STING pathway activation, Treg/M2 polarization, and PD-L1 expression. Although these microbial communities are conceptually linked through the lung-gut axis, the empirical evidence supporting their integrated network remains preliminary, and the clinical relevance of these interactions requires further investigation. Future research should focus on establishing causal relationships between specific microbial taxa and immunotherapy outcomes, elucidating spatial heterogeneity through multi-omics approaches, and validating microbiota-targeted interventions in well-designed prospective studies. This review offers a framework for critically evaluating the current evidence and identifying key knowledge gaps in this evolving field.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND AND AIM: The role of regulatory B cells (Bregs) cells and regulatory T cells (Tregs) has been little investigated in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Therefore, we investigated the frequency of circulating Bregs, Tregs cells, and the serum cytokine profile in NSCLC and their association with disease progression. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this prospective case-control study, peripheral blood from 40 patients with NSCLC and 40 healthy controls was examined, the frequency of various lymphocyte subsets including Bregs and Tregs was evaluated using flow cytometry. Serum cytokine profile including IL1β, IL6, IL-17, TNF-α, IL10, IL35 and TGF-β1 was measured using Luminex assay. RESULTS: An increased proportion of Bregs, Tregs, CD8 + T cells, and decreased CD4+/CD8 + ratio was observed in NSCLC patients compared to healthy controls. NSCLC patients with metastasis had a higher frequency of Bregs and Tregs than patients without metastasis. The frequency of Bregs and Tregs was related to the stage and histopathological status. NSCLC patients had significantly higher levels of serum cytokine profile when compared to healthy controls along with a significant association with lymph node metastasis and different TNM stages. CONCLUSIONS: Peripheral Bregs, Tregs, and serum cytokine profiles, including proinflammatory and anti-inflammatory cytokines were increased among NSCLC patients and may be associated with disease progression and metastasis.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Pneumothorax is the most common complication of computed tomography (CT)-guided transthoracic lung biopsy (TLB). Whether supplemental oxygen administered during the procedure before pneumothorax detection is associated with postprocedural pneumothorax remains unclear. This study evaluated the association between documented intraprocedural oxygen administration and postprocedural pneumothorax. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 442 consecutive patients who underwent CT-guided TLB between January 2022 and June 2025. Patients were grouped according to documented oxygen administration during the biopsy and before pneumothorax detection. Oxygen administration was non-standardized, and the exact dose and timing could not be reliably determined. Clinical, imaging, and procedural variables were evaluated. The primary outcome was postprocedural pneumothorax. Multivariable logistic regression analysis was performed to identify factors independently associated with pneumothorax. RESULTS: Intraprocedural oxygen administration was documented in 118 patients (26.7%), whereas 324 patients (73.3%) received no intraprocedural oxygen. Pneumothorax occurred in 141 patients (31.9%). The pneumothorax rate did not differ significantly between the oxygen and no-oxygen groups [36/118 (30.5%) vs. 105/324 (32.4%); absolute risk difference, - 1.9% points; 95% CI, - 11.6 to 7.8; p = 0.705]. No statistically significant association was identified between documented intraprocedural oxygen administration and postprocedural pneumothorax in the univariable analysis (OR, 0.916; 95% CI, 0.581-1.444; p = 0.705) or after multivariable adjustment (adjusted OR, 0.807; 95% CI, 0.492-1.323; p = 0.395). Non-pleural-based lesion location and CT-detected emphysema were independently associated with pneumothorax, whereas the association with lower subcutaneous tissue thickness should be considered exploratory. Pulmonary hemorrhage and pneumothorax-related intervention rates did not differ significantly between the groups. CONCLUSION: In this retrospective cohort, no statistically significant association was identified between documented intraprocedural oxygen administration and postprocedural pneumothorax after CT-guided TLB. This finding does not exclude a preventive effect, which should be evaluated in prospective studies using standardized oxygen protocols. CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

papers.abstract_en: AIMS: For patients with unresectable stage III non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) ineligible for concurrent chemo-radiation (cCRT), stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) may provide a favorable efficacy-toxicity balance. MATERIALS AND METHODS: STARLORD (STereotActic Radiotherapy for LOcally advanced non--small cell lung cancer ineligible for concurrent chemoRaDiation) is a prospective phase II study evaluating safety and early outcomes of SBRT after chemotherapy is delivered with Radixact system. RESULTS: Twenty-six consecutive patients with stage IIIB-IIIC NSCLC were analyzed with median age 75.5 years (IQR, 72.2-79.8), with 84.6% of patients presenting stage IIIB disease and 15.4% stage IIIC. Following induction chemotherapy, SBRT was delivered to both the primary tumor and mediastinal disease in 5 fractions, for median total doses, respectively, of 40 Gy (IQR, 40-45 Gy) and 35 Gy (IQR, 35-40 Gy). Consolidation immunotherapy was administered in 76.9% of patients. After a median follow-up of 17.3 months, acute grade 3 (G3) dysphagia was observed in 7.7%, no late grade ≥3 toxicities were observed. The 1-year local control (LC) rate was 86.7%, with two mediastinal progressions occurring 11 and 12 months after SBRT. Median distant progression-free survival (mDPFS) was 15.6 months with a 1-year DPFS rate of 56.7%. Four deaths were recorded during follow-up, resulting in a 1-year overall survival (OS) rate of 90.9%, with worse outcomes for patients with stage IIIC disease (log-rank P = .00027) and aged ≥75 years (log-rank P = .032). CONCLUSIONS: In our experience, for frailer patients with unresectable locally advanced NSCLC, SBRT is well tolerated and provides promising disease control outcomes.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Most patients with hypopharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (HPSCC) achieve partial response (PR) after induction chemotherapy. However, optimal post-induction management remains controversial. We compared survival outcomes of post-induction strategies for PR-HPSCC, with emphasis on advanced post-induction tumor stage (ycT) using inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW-ATO) to mitigate confounding by indication. METHODS: This retrospective study included 149 patients with PR-HPSCC after induction chemotherapy who subsequently received surgery-based therapy (SBT; n = 71) or definitive chemoradiotherapy (CRT; n = 78). IPTW-ATO was used to address covariate imbalances between groups. Overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) were evaluated using weighted Kaplan-Meier analyses and IPTW-ATO-adjusted Cox proportional hazards models. Sensitivity analyses compared findings across unadjusted, multivariable, and propensity score-weighted models. RESULTS: In unadjusted analyses, OS and PFS did not differ significantly between groups. After IPTW-ATO adjustment, SBT was associated with improved OS and PFS versus CRT. Exploratory subgroup analyses suggested a potential differential treatment effect across ycT strata; however, interaction tests were not statistically significant, and no significant survival difference was observed in patients with early ycT disease. In multivariable analyses, thyroid invasion was independently associated with worse OS, whereas anti-PD-1 therapy was associated with improved OS. CONCLUSIONS: Outcomes among patients with PR-HPSCC are heterogeneous. After adjustment for covariate imbalances, SBT was associated with favorable survival. These findings suggest that PR should not be treated as a uniform entity and that post-induction ycT classification may help stratify patients for future prospective evaluation.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Thymic epithelial tumors (TETs) are rare thoracic malignancies for which racial disparities in outcomes remain poorly characterized. We evaluated survival outcomes across racial groups and explored the clinical and sociodemographic factors that may help contextualize any observed differences. PATIENTS AND METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 128 consecutive patients with histologically confirmed TETs referred to the University of Chicago between January 1989 and March 2024. Associations between race, socioeconomic variables, and overall survival (OS) were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression, Cox proportional hazards models, and inverse probability of treatment weighting with average treatment effect (IPTW-ATE). RESULTS: Among 128 patients (75 White, 58%; 31 Black, 24%), Black race showed numerically worse OS on univariable analysis (hazard ratios [HR] 1.90, 95% confidence intervals [CI] 0.93-3.88; P = .077). Socioeconomic disparities were substantial: 74.2% of Black patients resided in low-income areas versus 12.2% of White patients (adjusted odds ratio 4.45, 95% CI 2.60-7.64; P < .0001). On multivariable analysis, thymic carcinoma histology (HR 3.97; P = .0012) and age older than 60 years (HR 2.19; P = .032) independently predicted worse survival. Black patients demonstrated numerically poorer OS (HR 2.49; P = .098). After IPTW-ATE adjustment, the association between Black race and OS was attenuated (HR 1.66, 95% CI 0.82-3.33; P = .157). CONCLUSION: Socioeconomic disadvantage emerged as one of several factors that may help contextualize the observed survival disparities in TETs. The attenuation of the effect estimates after adjustment for area-level socioeconomic factors suggests that social determinants of health may be relevant to the interpretation of these findings. Larger multi-institutional studies are needed to validate these observations.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is the most common form of lung cancer and is often diagnosed at an advanced stage, leading to poor prognosis. Carcinoembryonic antigen-related cell adhesion molecule 5 (CEACAM5) has emerged as a potential biomarker in colorectal and other gastrointestinal cancer; however, its role in NSCLC remains unexplored. This study evaluated the prognostic role of the CEACAM5 biomarker in metastatic non-squamous (mNSQ) NSCLC using real-world data. METHODS: CEACAM5 expression was assessed via immunohistochemistry of archival tissue from 336 eligible patients. Real-world overall survival (rwOS) was the primary outcome analyzed across six treatment cohorts. Secondary outcomes included prevalence of CEACAM5 expression (high, moderate, negative) by cohort and tumor site (primary vs. metastatic) and other outcomes including real-world progression-free survival (rwPFS), time to next treatment (rwTTNT), and time to treatment discontinuation (rwTTD). RESULTS: High CEACAM5 expression was observed in approximately 18% of the overall population, with consistent levels observed across both primary and metastatic tumor samples. No significant associations were found between different CEACAM5 expression levels and rwOS, rwPFS, rwTTNT, and rwTTD, across all cohorts. CONCLUSION: CEACAM5 did not demonstrate prognostic value in this retrospective cohort study of patients with metastatic NSCLC. Further research to confirm our findings is needed.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: COPD and vascular aging frequently coexist in later life. Whether widened pulse pressure identifies older adults with COPD at particularly high cardiovascular risk is uncertain. PATIENTS AND METHODS: We analyzed CHARLS participants aged 60 years or older without baseline heart disease or stroke. Questionnaire-defined COPD and widened pulse pressure (≥60 mmHg) formed four phenotypes. The primary outcome was incident physician-reported heart disease or stroke; all-cause mortality was secondary, and heart disease and stroke were component outcomes. Weighted cause-specific Cox models used respondent weights and household-cluster robust standard errors. Because the joint phenotype was selected after an exploratory screen of candidate vascular indicators, this study should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating rather than confirmatory. RESULTS: Among 4183 participants, 943 developed incident cardiovascular disease and 685 died. Relative to neither exposure, COPD alone (adjusted hazard ratio (HR) 1.15, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.84-1.57) and widened pulse pressure alone (HR 0.93, 95% CI 0.70-1.25) were not associated with cardiovascular disease, whereas both exposures were (HR 1.86, 95% CI 1.26-2.76). The cardiovascular association was present for heart disease (HR 2.80, 95% CI 1.94-4.05) but not stroke (HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.43-1.65). The composite cardiovascular signal should therefore not be read as a uniform effect across cardiovascular systems. For all-cause mortality, the both-exposure group had 63 deaths among 209 participants and a fully adjusted HR of 2.05 (95% CI 1.54-2.73) versus neither exposure, but mortality was not clearly higher than in the COPD-only group (HR 1.37, 95% CI 0.96-1.95). CONCLUSION: Coexisting questionnaire-defined COPD and widened pulse pressure was associated with a higher risk of incident cardiovascular disease, primarily reported heart disease, and with higher all-cause mortality than neither exposure, although mortality was not clearly higher than among participants with COPD alone. These findings are hypothesis-generating and warrant external validation using objective pulmonary and vascular measures.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is strongly linked to heart failure (HF), but comprehensive global evaluations of COPD-associated HF remain limited. METHODS: Using Global Burden of Disease Study 2021 data, we assessed prevalence and years lived with disability (YLDs) of COPD-associated HF. We applied decomposition analysis, Joinpoint regression, and Bayesian age-period-cohort modeling to evaluate trends by sex, age, sociodemographic index (SDI), and region, and to project burden to 2050. RESULTS: In 2021, global COPD-associated HF cases exceeded 3.61 million, a 1.4-fold increase since 1990. Age-standardized prevalence rates (ASPR) and YLD rates (ASYR) increased overall. Absolute cases and YLDs rose in both sexes, but age-standardized rates declined in males and rose in females. Burden peaked at ages 70-74 and grew fastest among those aged ≥95. The Middle SDI region had the highest counts; East Asia had the highest regional burden, and China the highest national absolute burden. Only High-SDI regions showed rising ASPR and ASYR; most other regions declined, notably Eastern Europe. Projections indicate global increases in ASPR and ASYR from 2022 to 2050, with slightly higher rises in females than males. CONCLUSION: The global burden of COPD-associated HF continues to rise with substantial heterogeneity and is projected to increase further. Coordinated international efforts and targeted prevention and management are urgently needed.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD) complicated by Type II respiratory failure frequently requires noninvasive ventilation (NIV). However, 10-25% of patients fail NIV and require intubation. The optimal timing and threshold of partial pressure of arterial carbon dioxide (PaCO2) for predicting NIV failure remain unclear. METHODS: In this two-center retrospective cohort study of 676 patients with AECOPD and Type II respiratory failure treated with NIV between 2012 and 2025, we used multivariable logistic regression and restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis (4 knots at the 5th, 35th, 65th, and 95th percentiles) to assess the dose-response relationship between 24-hour post-treatment PaCO2 and NIV failure. RESULTS: NIV failure occurred in 73 patients (10.8%). After full adjustment for age, heart rate, white blood cell count, hemoglobin, albumin, blood urea nitrogen, D-dimer, and baseline HACOR score, each 1 mmHg increase in 24h PaCO2 was associated with 3% higher odds of NIV failure (OR 1.03, 95% CI 1.01-1.06). RCS analysis revealed a nonlinear L-shaped association (overall P < 0.001; nonlinear P < 0.01), with a threshold at 60.2 mmHg. Below this threshold, no significant association was observed; above it, odds increased markedly; this threshold requires further external validation in independent patient populations. After adjustment for confounding variables, the fully‑adjusted multivariable model yielded an AUC of 0.805 (95% CI 0.751-0.860). CONCLUSION: A 24-hour post-treatment PaCO2 exceeding 60.2 mmHg identifies patients at high risk for NIV failure. This readily available bedside measure may guide escalation decisions in AECOPD with Type II respiratory failure.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Long waiting times on chemotherapy days increase patient burden. Pre-visit blood sampling may streamline workflows; however, its real-world impact remains unclear. METHODS: This prospective study collected data on waiting times for pre-visit vs same-day blood sampling in 50 cancer patients receiving chemotherapy between October 2024 and February 2025 at St. Marianna University Hospital. Pre‑visit and same‑day blood sampling was compared in the same patients across four waiting times: (i) check-in to consultation, (ii) check-in to check-out, and (iii-iv) extended measures incorporating travel time. For times (iii) and (iv), travel time during pre-visit was also included. Patient and physician satisfaction and indirect costs were also evaluated. RESULTS: The median waiting time from check-in to consultation was 1.8 and 2.2 h for pre-visit and same-day sampling, respectively; when chemotherapy and check-out were included (ii), total duration was similar (6.3 vs 6.3 h). Extended measures (iii-iv) tended to be longer with pre-visit sampling. After excluding the two outliers, waiting time from check-in to chemotherapy was significantly shorter for pre-visit vs same-day sampling (3.3 vs 3.9 h, p=0.025). Patient satisfaction was favorable, and 24.0% of patients reported reduced burden. Indirect costs improved by approximately 1198 Japanese yen per patient, with benefits reported in approximately half of the cases. Subgroup analyses suggested greater benefits for patients living within 30 min of both pre-visit blood sampling and chemotherapy facilities. CONCLUSIONS: Pre-visit blood sampling may reduce waiting time and perceived burden for selected patients, although overall time savings were modest. Trial registration University Hospital Medical Information Network (UMIN) Clinical Trials Registry: UMIN000055757.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Gastric cancer with duodenal invasion (Duo+) presents a distinct surgical challenge because adequate distal-margin clearance must be achieved without compromising duodenal stump safety. Standardised laparoscopic strategies for this setting remain poorly defined. METHODS: In this single-centre retrospective cohort study, we evaluated the technical feasibility and observed outcomes of an integrated extended-mobilisation and margin-control strategy in 500 patients undergoing laparoscopic distal gastrectomy with D2 lymphadenectomy for stage II-III gastric adenocarcinoma. The cohort included 90 patients with duodenal invasion (Duo+) and 410 without duodenal invasion (Duo-). In Duo+ cases, the strategy comprised extended duodenal-bulb mobilisation, optimisation of stapler angulation, routine intraoperative frozen-section diagnosis of the distal margin, and reinforcement of the duodenal stump. Outcomes in the Duo- group were reported to provide clinical context rather than to estimate the effect of the strategy relative to conventional mobilisation. RESULTS: Resected duodenal length was greater in Duo+ (median 3 vs 1cm; P<0.001); no distal-margin positivity in either group (0/90 vs 0/410). R0 rates were similar (95.6% vs 96.8%; P=0.78). Estimated blood loss did not differ (75 vs 55mL; P=0.18). Postoperative morbidity was numerically higher in Duo+ but not significant: Clavien-Dindo ≥II (40.0% vs 35.1%; P=0.38), ≥III (10.0% vs 7.1%; P=0.33), pancreatic fistula (5.6% vs 3.4%; P=0.42), duodenal stump fistula (2.2% vs 0.5%; P=0.17). Five-year overall survival was comparable (48% vs 52%; log-rank P=0.45). CONCLUSIONS: In this single-centre retrospective series, an integrated extended-mobilisation and margin-control strategy was feasible during laparoscopic distal gastrectomy for gastric cancer with duodenal invasion, and no distal-margin-positive cases were observed among the Duo+ patients. These descriptive findings do not establish superiority or equivalence relative to conventional mobilisation or identify the contribution of any individual component of the strategy. Comparative multicentre studies are required.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is the most sensitive non-invasive method for assessing joint lesions in juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA), but conventional protocols cannot simultaneously depict synovial inflammation and the associated vascular changes. OBJECTIVE: To assess changes in the "synovium-vascular axis" of the hand in children with JIA using 5.0-T MRI and contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance angiography (CE-MRA). MATERIALS AND METHODS: Twenty children with JIA and 10 age- and sex-matched healthy controls underwent hand 5.0-T MRI, including contrast-enhanced T1-weighted imaging and CE-MRA. The maximum synovial thickness, enhancement rate, bone marrow edema score, palmar digital artery diameter ratios, palmar arch integrity, distal microcirculation score, and vascular tortuosity were quantified. Correlations with the Juvenile Arthritis Disease Activity Score-27 (JADAS-27), erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), and C-reactive protein (CRP) were analyzed. RESULTS: Compared with controls, the JIA group showed higher maximum synovial thickness (5.19±2.35 mm vs. 0.83±0.24 mm, P<0.001), enhancement rate (0.44±0.20 vs. 0.20±0.14, P=0.002), bone marrow edema score (median 7.50 vs. 0, P<0.001), and vascular tortuosity (2.0 vs. 0, P<0.001), but lower common palmar digital artery diameter ratio (0.690 vs. 1.000, P<0.001) and microcirculation score (1.0 vs. 3.0, P<0.001). The bone marrow edema score (r=0.674, P=0.001), maximum synovial thickness (r=0.581, P=0.007), and enhancement rate (r=0.634, P=0.003) correlated positively with JADAS-27, and the bone marrow edema score was independently associated with ln(JADAS-27) (standardized β=0.677, P=0.005). CONCLUSION: Combined 5.0-T MRI and CE-MRA revealed a distinct pattern of synovial inflammation, arterial narrowing, and impaired distal microcirculatory perfusion in children with JIA. CE-MRA-derived vascular parameters are candidate exploratory imaging markers requiring validation in larger multicenter cohorts.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Multiple instruments are used to assess fecal continence and bowel function after anorectal malformation (ARM) repair, but their comparability is uncertain. This systematic review examined inter-system agreement and differences in the findings produced when two or more scoring systems were applied to the same ARM cohort. METHODS: MEDLINE, Embase, and Web of Science were searched from inception through 26 April 2026. Original studies applying at least two named fecal continence or bowel function scoring systems to the same ARM cohort were eligible. Risk of bias was assessed using an adapted QUADAS-2 framework. Because comparable agreement estimates were sparse, results were synthesized narratively (PROSPERO: CRD420261377404). RESULTS: Fifteen studies published from 2012 to 2025, with individual sample sizes of 20-267 participants, were included. Krickenbeck was used in 14 studies (93%) and Kelly in nine (60%). Only one study, based on 39 parent-reported assessments, reported numerical inter-system agreement estimates; weighted κ values for four score pairs ranged from 0.256 to 0.343. Other studies described category discordance or differences in group-level findings. In one cohort, Kelly did not identify a between-group difference detected by Krickenbeck and Rintala. In another small cohort, Kelly continence and the Krickenbeck constipation domain favored different surgical groups, although they assessed different outcome constructs. Blinding between instrument administrations was unreported in 12 studies. CONCLUSION: The limited available evidence suggests that commonly used ARM bowel function instruments may yield non-equivalent information, but it is insufficient to establish their interchangeability or the superiority of any single system. Krickenbeck is currently the most frequently used instrument. Prospective comparative studies using standardized administration and appropriate agreement analyses are needed before a universal core instrument can be recommended.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The use of inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) in bronchiectasis patients with eosinophilic inflammation is controversial due to the potential risk of bronchial or pulmonary infection. This study examined the association between ICS use and first Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolation across strata of blood eosinophil count (BEC). METHODS: A multicenter retrospective study was conducted in patients with bronchiectasis, who were classified according to baseline BEC at cohort entry: HighBEC (≥ 300 cells/μL), InterBEC (100-299 cells/μL), and LowBEC (< 100 cells/μL). ICS use was identified from prescription records, and first P. aeruginosa isolation was defined as the first positive culture for P. aeruginosa from a lower respiratory tract sample after cohort entry. Multivariate Cox proportional hazards regression was used to quantify the risk of first P. aeruginosa isolation associated with ICS use. RESULTS: Of 1,900 bronchiectasis patients assessed, 719 were analyzed: 194 (27.0%) received ICS, 525 (73.0%) did not. During follow-up, P. aeruginosa was detected in 69 (9.6%) patients. After adjustment for potential confounders and disease severity indicators, ICS use was associated with a significantly higher risk of first P. aeruginosa isolation in patients with BEC ≥ 100 cells/μL, using no ICS as reference (HighBEC: adjusted HR 4.15, 95% CI 1.29-13.38, P = 0.0172; InterBEC: adjusted HR 3.13, 95% CI 1.56-6.27, P = 0.0013), but not in LowBEC patients (adjusted HR 0.48, 95% CI 0.08-2.79, P = 0.4160). Propensity-matched analyses supported these findings. CONCLUSION: ICS use was associated with an increased risk of first P. aeruginosa isolation in eosinophilic bronchiectasis, suggesting caution when prescribing ICS to these patients.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Guided by Rapid Evaluation and Assessment Methods (REAM) and using rigorous quality improvement processes, we describe implementation of an evidence-based psychosocial screening program at key transitions in childhood cancer treatment to guide care matched to need. METHODS: Pediatric cancer patients (≥ 11 years) and caregivers (patients 0-17 years) were offered screening questionnaires electronically at 4-6 months, 18-24 months, and 4-6 years post-diagnosis through a phased implementation across three cancer center sites and in their preferred language (English, Spanish, Arabic). Screening questionnaires assessed cancer-related symptoms, health-related quality of life, cognitive function and school needs, caregiver adjustment and family risk, and resource needs. To assess adoption, feasibility, penetration, and sustainability, data related to screening processes, documentation completion rates, and adaptations were tracked and summarized. Qualitative interviews with patients, caregivers, and clinicians, based on the Consolidated Framework for Intervention Research (CFIR), were coded for acceptability and screening program optimization. RESULTS: Across sites and timepoints, from June 2023 through November 2025, there was a 56% screening completion rate (470/846). Patient physical functioning, emotional functioning, and neurocognitive functioning, caregiver adjustment, and resource needs were consistently flagged for follow-up. Documentation of follow-up varied with rates of 74% for social workers and 34% for medical clinicians. Patients, caregivers, and clinicians endorsed moderate acceptability. Barriers to electronic health record integration complicated clinician workflows. From initiation, over 2 years, 55 adaptations were made to improve workflow, implementation strategies, screening processes, and measures. CONCLUSION: We achieved development, implementation, and optimization of a psychosocial screening program across our cancer center.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Rehabilitation nursing plays a critical role in supporting postoperative functional recovery and facilitating reintegration into daily life and work, yet evidence on factors associated with early return to work (RTW) among young and middle-aged patients with lung cancer remains limited. This study aimed to examine the associations of in-hospital recovery, cancer self-management self-efficacy, and perceived social support with early RTW at 1 month after surgery among young and middle-aged patients with lung cancer. METHODS: This prospective cohort study recruited 160 young and middle-aged adults who underwent minimally invasive lung cancer surgery at a tertiary hospital in Shanghai from June to December 2024. Before discharge, participants completed baseline assessments including the Quality of Recovery-15 scale, the Strategies Used by People to Promote Health, and the Perceived Social Support Scale. RTW status and RTW stage were assessed 1 month postoperatively. Binary logistic regression was used to examine factors associated with early RTW. RESULTS: Among the 160 participants, 88 (55%) had returned to work 1 month after surgery, while 72 (45%) had not. Of those who returned to work, 53 were categorized into the "uncertain maintenance" stage and 35 into the "proactive maintenance" stage. Non-RTW participants were distributed across the "precontemplation" (n = 9), "contemplation" (n = 15), "prepared for action-self-evaluative" (n = 22), and "prepared for action-behavioural" (n = 26) stages. Higher levels of in-hospital recovery quality, self-efficacy, and perceived social support were significantly associated with an increased likelihood of early RTW. CONCLUSION: More than half of young and middle-aged lung cancer patients resumed work within 1 month after surgery; however, most remained in the "uncertain maintenance" stage. Better postoperative recovery, higher cancer self-management self-efficacy, and stronger perceived social support were associated with a greater likelihood of RTW at 1 month after surgery in this population. CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

papers.abstract_en: Objective: This study evaluated the diagnostic value of a combined SHOX2 and RASSF1A methylation assay (LungMe®) in differentiating malignant from benign pleural and peritoneal effusions. Methods: A total of 696 patients with pleural or peritoneal effusions were prospectively enrolled. Effusion sediment samples were analyzed by liquid-based cytology (TCT), cell block histology, and methylation-specific PCR for both SHOX2 and RASSF1A. The final diagnosis was confirmed by clinical, imaging, and pathological follow-up. Results: Lung cancer was the predominant cause of malignant pleural effusions (71.96%), while malignant peritoneal effusions mainly resulted from ovarian, gastric, and liver cancers. The optimal ΔCt cutoffs for SHOX2 and RASSF1A were ΔCt ≤ 9 and ΔCt ≤ 12, respectively. The combined methylation assay achieved a sensitivity of 79.1% and specificity of 90.4% for malignant effusions. When combined with cytology, the overall sensitivity increased from 34.7% (TCT alone) to 91.7%, with a positive predictive value (PPV) of 93.9% and a negative predictive value (NPV) of 86.7%. The assay showed high sensitivity across multiple tumor types, including 100% for esophageal and breast cancers, and ≥80% for lung cancer, gastric cancer, lymphoma, and cholangiocarcinoma. Conclusions: The combined SHOX2 and RASSF1A methylation assay has high diagnostic value for benign-malignant discrimination of pleural and peritoneal effusions, improving diagnostic sensitivity when combined with conventional cytology. Thus, within the context of this single-center study, the LungMe® assay demonstrates promise in expanding pan-cancer diagnostics, but will require further multicenter external validation and prospective clinical studies before routine clinical adoption.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Brain metastases are the most common malignant intracranial tumors and remain associated with poor survival despite advances in multimodal treatment. This study aimed to evaluate the associations between clinical, radiological, surgical, and perioperative characteristics and outcomes in patients undergoing surgical resection of brain metastases. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort study included 378 consecutive adult patients who underwent resection of histopathologically confirmed brain metastases between 2015 and 2023. Overall survival was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method, and differences between groups were assessed using the log-rank test. Factors associated with overall survival were evaluated using univariable and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression. Binary logistic regression was used to evaluate factors associated with 30-day mortality. RESULTS: Median overall survival was 11.3 months, the one-year survival rate was 45.5%, and 18 patients (4.8%) died within 30 days after surgery. In the adjusted logistic regression model, preoperative KPS < 80, hydrocephalus, postoperative hematoma, and postoperative pneumonia were associated with higher odds of 30-day mortality. In the multivariable Cox regression analysis, increasing age, preoperative KPS < 80, tumor volume ≥ 9 cm3, hydrocephalus, wound complications, and postoperative KPS deterioration were independently associated with shorter overall survival. Subtotal versus total resection was not significantly associated with overall survival after adjustment. CONCLUSIONS: Several preoperative and postoperative characteristics were associated with early mortality and overall survival in this surgically selected cohort. These findings emphasize the importance of careful patient selection, preservation of functional status, optimization of perioperative care, and prevention of postoperative complications.

papers.abstract_en: Background/Objectives: Accurate preoperative feeding artery mapping remains challenging for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) even with modern CT techniques. This study aimed to optimize dynamic multi-phase photon-counting CT (PCCT) hepatic artery protocols and assess dynamic-fusion PCCT against best single-phase PCCT and energy-integrating-detector dual-energy CT (EID-DECT) for feeding artery detection, vascular-map construction and digital subtraction angiography (DSA) path-planning prior to transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) in HCC. Methods: This prospective single-center study contained workflow-optimization among cirrhotic non-HCC patients and clinical validation in TACE-candidate HCC patients. Two radiologists performed blinded independent reading. The composite reference standard consisted of DSA, selective/superselective angiography, available cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) and embolization records. Primary endpoint: patient-level paired difference in DSA-verified feeding artery coverage. Secondary endpoints included complete-atlas rate, DSA-path-prediction accuracy, missed-vessel count and extrahepatic-supply detection. A pre-specified comparison between dynamic-fusion PCCT and EID-DECT was performed. Results: Dynamic phase 1-6 fusion was the optimal PCCT scheme, while optimal single-phase varied individually. Dynamic-fusion PCCT achieved superior feeding artery coverage (97.78% ± 8.61% vs. 88.33% ± 15.37%, difference 9.44 pp, 95% CI 1.82-17.06, p = 0.016), complete-atlas rate (93.3% vs. 53.3%, p = 0.039) and path-prediction accuracy (96.67% ± 11.18% vs. 80.00% ± 24.49%), with fewer missed culprit vessels. Two extrahepatic feeders were only detected by dynamic-fusion PCCT. Compared with EID-DECT, dynamic-fusion PCCT showed favorable atlas-related metrics without statistically significant difference in feeding artery coverage. Conclusions: Dynamic-fusion PCCT outperforms single-phase PCCT in pre-TACE feeding artery mapping and DSA path-prediction and shows potential benefits over EID-DECT. It delivers comprehensive preoperative vascular data and may reduce intraoperative exploratory procedures.

papers.abstract_en: Intestinal homeostasis requires tight regulation of stem cell maintenance and differentiation to absorptive and secretory cell types, two major intestinal lineages. Key signaling pathways have been identified, but how they balance cell type composition remains unclear. We uncovered oscillatory expression of the Notch-target protein Hes1 (hairy and enhancer of split 1) that controls cell fate specification in a frequency-dependent manner. An endogenous fluorescent Hes1 reporter revealed distinct, cell type-specific oscillation frequencies forming a gradient along the crypt-villus axis, which was modulated by cell cycle phase as well as Wnt (wingless-related integration site)-signaling and Notch-signaling activity. We developed a microfluidic system to modulate Notch-signaling oscillations in organoids and found the oscillation frequency to regulate the balance of cell type composition. This study provides evidence that information for cell fate specification is encoded in the frequency of an oscillatory signal.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains the leading cause of cancer mortality, and resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) is largely driven by the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME), in which tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) are major regulators. OBJECTIVES: This review summarizes recent advances in understanding TAM heterogeneity, their contribution to immune resistance in NSCLC, and emerging therapeutic strategies targeting TAMs. METHODS: A literature search was conducted using PubMed and Google Scholar, focusing on studies published between 2021 and 2025. Key search terms included "non-small cell lung cancer", "tumor immune microenvironment", "macrophage heterogeneity", "M1 macrophages", "M2 macrophages", "SPP1+ macrophages", "TREM2+ macrophages", "immune checkpoint inhibitor resistance", "macrophage metabolic reprogramming", and "TAM-targeted therapies". Relevant studies addressing TAM heterogeneity, immune resistance, metabolic and molecular regulation, and therapeutic targeting in NSCLC were prioritized, while earlier studies were included where necessary to provide mechanistic context. RESULTS: Recent evidence demonstrates that TAMs comprise diverse functional subsets rather than a simple M1/M2 duality. Distinct populations including CXCL9+, SPP1+, C1Q+, and TREM2+ macrophages differentially regulate T-cell exclusion, immune checkpoint resistance, angiogenesis, and metabolic remodeling. Therapeutic approaches targeting CSF1R, CD47-SIRPα, metabolic pathways, nanoparticles, epigenetic regulators, engineered macrophages, and microRNA-based strategies show promise but remain limited by macrophage plasticity and compensatory immune mechanisms. CONCLUSION: A comprehensive understanding of TAM heterogeneity within the tumor immune microenvironment provides a framework for overcoming immune resistance in NSCLC. Future therapeutic strategies should integrate biomarker-guided patient selection with combination approaches that simultaneously target macrophage plasticity and immune suppression.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Critically ill patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and sepsis are at high risk of in-hospital mortality because of respiratory and organ dysfunction. Early risk assessment may be useful for clinical decision-making. This study aimed to develop an interpretable machine learning model for this population. METHODS: Data were extracted from MIMIC-IV and the eICU Collaborative Research Database (eICU-CRD). The MIMIC-IV cohort was split in a 7:3 ratio into training and internal test sets. Features were selected using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression and Boruta. Eight models were trained using 10-fold cross-validation and grid search. The best-performing model was externally validated using eICU-CRD, interpreted using Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP), and compared with the Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score. RESULTS: Among 4,900 MIMIC-IV patients, in-hospital mortality was 19.2%. In the internal test set, the naive Bayes (NB) model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.743 (95% CI, 0.711-0.775), outperforming the SOFA score (AUC, 0.696, 95% CI, 0.663-0.730, P < 0.001). In external validation, AUC decreased to 0.681 (95% CI, 0.607-0.755), an absolute reduction of 0.062. SHAP identified Simplified Acute Physiology Score II and SOFA as predictors, followed by the anion gap and urine output. The model was deployed across web, desktop, and mobile platforms. CONCLUSION: An NB model was successfully developed to predict in-hospital mortality in critically ill patients with COPD and sepsis. Further prospective multicenter validation is warranted before routine clinical use.

papers.abstract_en: The rapid accumulation of multi-omics data provides increasing opportunities for cancer biomarker discovery, but the heterogeneity and high dimensionality of these datasets remain major challenges for data integration and analysis. This review examines the application of bioinformatics and artificial intelligence for multi-omics integration in cancer biomarker research. Common multi-omics data paradigms and integration strategies are discussed, followed by a review of the bioinformatics, machine learning and deep learning approaches applied across 84 included studies. Cross-study comparison showed limited recurrence among the reported biomarkers, with only 15 biomarkers identified in at least four studies. Further assessment of the 13 recurrent protein-coding biomarkers showed significant protein-protein interaction enrichment and functional convergence in cancer-related processes, particularly PI3K/AKT and ERBB2-related signaling. This review also highlights current challenges, including missing data, heterogeneity across datasets, limited independent validation and the interpretability of artificial intelligence models. Future research may benefit from integrating multi-omics data with clinical information, pathological imaging, electronic health records, single-cell multi-omics and radiomics, together with broader datasets and greater use of independent validation to support the translation of multi-omics biomarker findings into clinical applications.

papers.abstract_en: Background/Objectives: Glutathione S-transferase theta 2 (GSTT2) is highly expressed in esophageal tissues from African American (AA) compared with European American (EA) individuals, but its localization, regulation, and relevance to esophageal adenocarcinoma progression remain unclear. Methods: Here, we combined FISH, immunofluorescence, patient-derived culture models, cell-cycle synchronization, biochemical perturbation, and transcriptomics to define GSTT2 expression in normal and neoplastic esophageal contexts. Results: In developing and adult esophageal tissues, GSTT2 mRNA and protein were broadly distributed across squamous epithelium and lamina propria, co-localizing with p63-positive basal/progenitor cells and extending into differentiated compartments, with no major ancestry-associated differences in spatial patterning. In Barrett's esophagus, GSTT2 protein was retained in metaplastic columnar epithelium and slightly elevated in dysplastic versus adjacent non-dysplastic regions. GSTT2 mRNA was highest in normal squamous esophagus, reduced during Barrett's-to-adenocarcinoma progression, but increased in treatment-resistant esophageal adenocarcinoma (EAC). In resistant EAC, GSTT2 co-expression shifted from homeostatic antioxidant programs to proliferation and mitotic pathways, including the G2-M checkpoint, E2F targets, and Reactome Cell Cycle, with leading-edge regulators CDK1 and CDC20. Sequence analysis identified putative APC-C and FBXW7 recognition motifs. In synchronized cells, GSTT2 abundance declined during S-G2/M and increased during mitotic exit/early G1 in cytosolic and membrane fractions. Forskolin, a dual inhibitor of FBXW7 and CDC20, stabilized GSTT2 and rescued CDC20- or FBXW7-associated loss, implicating APC-CDC20 and FBXW7 pathways in GSTT2 turnover. In EAC cells, by contrast, CDC20 was found to be a cooperative partner stabilizing GSTT2. Conclusions: These findings identify GSTT2 as a spatially widespread, ancestry-associated, cell-cycle-regulated protein with potential oncogenic roles in EAC resistance.

papers.abstract_en: Partially methylated domains (PMDs) represent extensive genome-wide hypomethylated regions that drive genomic instability and proto-oncogene activation. However, their complex regulatory influence on tumor-specific transcriptional networks remains largely elusive. In this study, we developed a robust computational pipeline to characterize aberrant PMD landscapes across pan-cancer. We specifically focused on the epigenetic features associated with transcriptional dysregulation in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). By analyzing gene expression patterns, we classified PMDs into four distinct classes and revealed that several immunosuppressive genes were recurrently activated within Tumor-PMDs across various cancers. While these PMDs were generally marked by elevated repressive H3K27me3 and diminished active histone modifications, the activated genes within them paradoxically exhibited a precise, localized enrichment of H3K9ac and H3K27ac near their transcription start sites (TSSs). This localized epigenetic rewiring suggests a potential correlation where collaborative histone modification landscapes may shape oncogenic chromatin remodeling to license transcriptional dysregulation. Furthermore, we identified a robust co-expression axis between the prognostic gene ATP6V0D2 and established immune checkpoints (HAVCR2, TDO2). Elevated ATP6V0D2 expression was found to potentially contribute to ESCC progression and poor prognosis by activating the complement system and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) pathways. Capitalizing on these findings, virtual screening and in vitro validation suggested that caffeic acid could act as a potential ATP6V0D2-binding compound, effectively suppressing the migration and viability of ESCC cells. This study further nominates caffeic acid as a candidate compound for further mechanistic and therapeutic investigation in ESCC.

papers.abstract_en: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains a leading cause of cancer‑related mortality, and mitochondrial proteins have been increasingly implicated in tumor progression. Coiled‑coil‑helix‑coiled‑coil‑helix domain‑containing 2 (CHCHD2) has been reported in several malignancies, yet its pan‑cancer landscape and LUAD‑specific functional relevance have not been comprehensively evaluated. In the present study, multi‑omics analyses were integrated using The Cancer Genome Atlas‑derived datasets and public resources [including Gene Expression Profiling Interactive Analysis (GEPIA) 2, CIBERSORT and CellMiner] to characterize CHCHD2 expression patterns, clinical associations, tumor microenvironment (TME) features, stemness‑related indices and drug‑response correlations across cancers, followed by experimental validation in LUAD models. CHCHD2 was found to be upregulated in multiple cancers and was correlated with advanced disease stage and poor overall survival, especially in patients with LUAD. CHCHD2 promoted cell proliferation and migration while inhibiting apoptosis. CHCHD2 knockdown reduced AKT and ERK phosphorylation and suppressed xenograft tumor growth in vivo. High CHCHD2 expression was associated with increased stemness, an immunosuppressive TME, and differential drug‑response patterns in CellMiner analyses, suggesting that CHCHD2 expression may be associated with compound‑specific sensitivity profiles. Collectively, these findings support an oncogenic role of CHCHD2 in LUAD and highlight its potential utility as a prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: Acute reactions to iodinated contrast material (ICM) and gadolinium-based contrast agents (GBCAs) are routinely encountered during CT and MR exams, but their associated direct medical costs and radiology practice workflow delays remain largely unknown. The purpose of this five-year, single-center retrospective study was to determine the costs and the Radiology departmental delays associated with acute ICM and GBCA reactions. METHODS: Contrast-enhanced CT and MR (CECT and CEMR) examinations performed from November 1, 2019, to October 31, 2024 at our institution were included. Acute reactions were identified as allergic-like or physiologic and categorized by severity using established ACR criteria. Drug, procedural, and hospitalization costs were estimated using 2025 CMS and US Department of Veterans Affairs databases. Delays were quantified by comparing time from exam start to departmental exit for exams with and without reactions. RESULTS: A total of 363,671 CECT exams and 253,860 CEMR exams were included, with 1099 acute ICM (789 allergic-like, 310 physiologic) and 521 acute GBCA reactions (321 allergic-like, 200 physiologic) identified. A minority of patients received billable medication or a procedure for their treatment (321 CECT, 29%; 107 CEMR, 21%). Median costs were modest ($15 for CECT; $1.66 for CEMR), but varied substantially by severity (severe reactions up to $238,029) and outcome (ED patient = $326, Admitted patient = $13,942). Acute ICM and GBCA reactions resulted in a median additional time of 25 minutes (IQR 11-43 min) and 27 minutes (IQR 8-59 min) in Radiology, respectively. CONCLUSION: Acute ICM and GBCA reactions contribute to additional estimated direct medical costs and imaging delays that increase with reaction severity. Our findings help quantify how these adverse events increase direct and indirect estimated direct medical costs and negatively affect Radiology workflow; providing decision makers with important economic and operational context.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Tislelizumab and Sintilimab are commonly used immunotherapy drugs in clinical practice. Only a portion of advanced NSCLC patients achieve sustained remission and long-term survival through ICI immunotherapy, while others experience disease progression post-treatment. Selecting appropriate clinical therapies and predicting treatment efficacy remain significant challenges in clinical practice. By examining the clinical efficacy and safety of tislelizumab and sintilimab combined with chemotherapy in advanced NSCLC patients within real-world settings, and analyzing prognostic factors, this study aims to provide reference for clinical treatment decisions and prognosis assessment. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective analysis of clinical data from 212 patients with advanced NSCLC treated with the combination of tislelizumab or sintilimab plus chemotherapy in The First Affiliated Hospital of Dali University between March 1, 2022, and December 31, 2024. Patients were divided into the tislelizumab group (n = 124) and the sintilimab group (n = 88) based on the administered drug. Objective response rate (ORR), disease control rate (DCR), progression-free survival (PFS), and overall survival (OS) were evaluated in both groups. Kaplan-Meier methods were used to plot PFS and OS survival curves. Univariate analysis was performed using the Log-rank test, and Cox regression models were employed to identify independent prognostic factors for PFS and OS. RESULTS: The median progression-free survival (mPFS) in the tislelizumab group and the sintilimab group was 14.0 months (95% CI: 11.79-16.21) and 7.0 months (95% CI: 4.31-9.69), respectively (P = 0.005). The difference in mPFS between the two groups was statistically significant. The median overall survival (mOS) was 27.0 months (95% CI: 20.03-33.97) and 24.0 months (95% CI: 13.85-34.15) (P = 0.113), with no statistically significant difference in mOS between groups. ORR was 39.52% versus 18.18% (P < 0.001), showing a statistically significant difference; DCR was 66.13% versus 70.54% (P = 0.506), with no statistically significant difference. After adjustment for confounders, multivariable Cox regression revealed no significant differences between the two agents for PFS (HR = 1.128, 95% CI 0.596-2.133, P = 0.712) or OS (HR = 0.664, 95% CI 0.378-1.165, P = 0.153). ADR occurrence showed a borderline association with improved OS (HR = 0.569, P = 0.093), but was not statistically significant. ALI, PNI, anti-angiogenic combination, and treatment line were not independent prognostic factors (all P > 0.05). CONCLUSION: In real-world clinical settings, tislelizumab combined with chemotherapy may bring potential improvements in objective response rate and progression-free survival in the short term for patients with advanced NSCLC. Nevertheless, sintilimab and tislelizumab exert comparable long-term survival benefits when used in combination with chemotherapy. After adjusting for confounding factors via multivariable regression analysis, no significant survival differences were confirmed between the two treatment regimens. Further prospective clinical studies with longer follow-up are required to verify the above conclusions.
