papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the role of the vascularized nasoseptal flap (VNSF) and septal flip flap (SFF) in anterior skull base (ASB) reconstruction of craniofacial therapy by studying the radioanatomy of VNSF, SFF and ASB reconstruction data on adult Computed Tomography (CT) multiplanar reconstruction. METHODS: The length, width and area of VNSF, SFF, and ASB defects were measured by Computed Tomography CT in 40 adults, and then the above date were statistically analyzed to confirm whether VNSF and SFF can be used to cover the ASB defect region produced after surgery. RESULTS: The area of VNSF far exceeded that of ASB defect (10.21 ± 1.97 cm2), and the anterior and posterior widths, as well as the upper and lower lengths of VNSF were at least 8.4 mm longer than the corresponding width and length of ASB defect to be reconstructed. The VNSF containing vascular pedicle had a total length exceed that required for ASB reconstruction via the anterior wall of the sphenoid sinus (SS) by at least 17.6 mm, but a mean length that was 7.02 ± 8.71 mm less than that required for transsphenoidal reconstruction of ASB. The area of SFF far exceeded that of the ASB defect (8.93 ± 1.49 cm2). The anterior and posterior widths, as well as the lower length of SFF all exceeded the corresponding width and length of the ASB defect to be reconstructed by at least 8.4 mm, and the upper length exceeded the ASB defect length by at least 1.5 mm. The independent sample t test showed no difference between sexes. Pearson correlation analysis showed no age difference except for the difference between SFF anterior width and ASB anterior width (P = 0.016). VNSF can reconstruct the defect of ASB through the anterior wall of the SS. CONCLUSION: With the assistance of SS packing and other methods, VNSF can transsphenoidally reconstruct the defect of the ASB, and SFF can reconstruct the defect of the ASB.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Prostate cancer burden may be amplified in rural regions or Appalachia areas, where access to screening and healthcare may be limited. This study examined geographic disparities and temporal trends in aggressive and metastatic prostate cancer across four groups defined by rurality and Appalachian status, while assessing assessed racial differences. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective study using the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) including newly diagnosed prostate cancer men aged ≥40 years (2004-2022). Age-adjusted incidences of more aggressive and metastatic cases were estimated for each geographical region. Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate geographic and racial disparities in risk of more aggressive cases, adjusting for demographic and clinical factors. RESULTS: We identified 951,965 eligible cases. Overall prostate cancer incidence declined in most regions, with a decrease in rural Appalachia (Annual percent changes [APC] = - 1.7%; 95% CI: [- 2.98%, - 0.42%]). Incidence of more aggressive cases increased over time particularly in urban Appalachia (APC = 2.73%; 95% CI: [1.20%, 4.65%]). For metastatic cases, urban Appalachia had the lowest overall incidence and rural non-Appalachia the highest, and rates increased across regions after 2020. In multivariable regression, geographic patterns differed by race. Among White men, compared with urban non-Appalachia, the odds of more aggressive prostate cancer were higher in rural non-Appalachia and rural Appalachia but lower in urban Appalachia. However, among Black men, those residing in rural Appalachia had significantly lower odds than those residing in urban non-Appalachia. Older age, Hispanic ethnicity, higher serum PSA, and lymph node-positive status were also associated with higher odds of more aggressive prostate cancer. CONCLUSION: Prostate cancer burden and severity varied by Appalachian status and rurality, supporting targeted, region- and race-specific strategies to improve early detection and access to high-quality care.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: This study evaluated the technical and procedural feasibility of MRI-guided stent implantation for CoA using a structured multistage preclinical evaluation protocol. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A commercially available MR Conditional guidewire and dedicated research prototypes comprising nitinol stents, delivery systems, and balloon catheters were assessed in a three-stage protocol. Device visibility was evaluated in a standardized water phantom at 1.5 T and 3.0 T. In a polymer-based CoA vessel phantom, 10 stent implantations were performed by novices (n = 6) and experts (n = 4), with four separate expert-led balloon dilatations. MRI-guided stent implantation was subsequently performed in five porcine models. RESULTS: All devices were visible at both field strengths, with lateral artifact widths of 5.3-7.8 mm for the guidewire, 20.9-38.5 mm for the stent delivery system, 13.1-19.9 mm for the expanded stents, and 17.4-30.5 mm for the balloon catheter. Phantom stenting duration was 10.2 ± 7.2 mins for novices and 6.2 ± 2.7 mins for experts. MRI-guided stent implantation was successfully performed in all five animals, with a mean duration of 13.6 ± 7.5 mins. In one animal, balloon post-dilatation was additionally performed as a procedural proof of concept. CONCLUSION: MRI-guided stent implantation for CoA is feasible within a structured multistage preclinical evaluation protocol and supports further clinical translation of radiation-free endovascular treatment.

papers.abstract_en: Immune dysregulation is central to acute myeloid leukemia (AML), but the contribution of specific immune subsets remains uncertain. We combined Mendelian randomization (MR), clinical flow cytometry, and transcriptomic profiling to investigate HLA-DR+ CD8+ T cells in AML. Two-sample MR using 731 immunophenotypes and AML data from UK Biobank and FinnGen identified four HLA-DR-related T-cell traits associated with lower AML susceptibility. In 85 non-APL patients, HLA-DR+ CD8+ T-cell proportions increased after complete remission, while among 46 newly diagnosed patients, a lower baseline HLA-DR+ CD8+ T-cell proportion was associated with poorer overall survival after adjustment for age and ELN risk category (HR 3.32, 95% CI 1.09-10.16, P = 0.035). A nomogram incorporating clinical and immune variables stratified patient risk. Transcriptomic analysis linked lower HLA-DR+ CD8+ T-cell levels to ribosomal and extracellular matrix pathways. These findings support HLA-DR+ CD8+ T cells as a favorable immune biomarker and clinically relevant immune correlate in AML.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: Mesothelioma mortality continues to reflect asbestos exposure because of its long latency. While previous Spanish studies focused primarily on pleural disease, this study assessed mesothelioma mortality across the ICD-10 C45 category in Spain from 1999 to 2024. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A population-based time-trend study was conducted using mortality data (ICD-10 C45) from the Spanish National Statistics Institute. Age-standardised mortality rates (ASMRs) were calculated using the 2013 European Standard Population. Temporal trends and sex-specific parallelism were evaluated using Joinpoint regression. RESULTS: Among 9733 recorded mesothelioma deaths (7311 men, 2422 women), ASMRs were consistently higher in men, although temporal trends were parallel by sex. Overall mortality increased until 2016 (annual percentage change [APC] 2.3%, 95% CI 1.5-3.0) and subsequently declined non-significantly, yielding an average annual percentage change (AAPC) of 1.0% (95% CI 0.2-1.7) for 1999-2024. Pleural mortality increased until 2011 before declining non-significantly, whereas recorded peritoneal mortality increased throughout the study period (AAPC 2.0%, 95% CI 0.7-3.2). Deaths coded as unspecified site (C45.9) showed the largest increase in ASMR (AAPC 2.1%, 95% CI 1.1-3.1) and accounted for 43.5% of male and 31.8% of female mesothelioma deaths in 2024. CONCLUSIONS: Absolute mesothelioma deaths increased in Spain while age-standardised rates attenuated after 2016. The continued increase in recorded peritoneal mortality and the substantial contribution of unspecified-site deaths indicate that surveillance should not rely solely on pleural mesothelioma, highlighting the need for comprehensive monitoring of the complete ICD-10 C45 category and improved anatomical classification.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. However, comprehensive population-level data describing etiologic patterns, treatment exposure, healthcare utilisation, and survival remain limited in many countries. This study aimed to characterise the national burden, care patterns, and outcomes of HCC in Turkey. METHODS: We performed a nationwide, real-world analysis of adult patients diagnosed with HCC between 2016 and 2024 using administrative health data. Cases were identified by an administrative case definition requiring at least three separate records of ICD-10 codes C22, C22.0, or C22.9; at least one C22.0 code was not required, so HCC could not be confirmed at the individual level. Baseline comorbidities were restricted to conditions recorded on or before the date of diagnosis. Demographic characteristics, underlying liver disease, etiologic factors, treatment exposure, and the level and type of diagnosing institution were assessed. Overall survival (OS) was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method. To reduce immortal-time bias, treatment exposure was analysed in a three-month landmark cohort; because treatment dates were unavailable, this reduces but does not eliminate the bias. Multivariable Cox regression was performed within the same cohort. RESULTS: A total of 13,674 patients (64.6% male; median age 64 years, IQR 55-73) were included, of whom 61.4% had died at the data cutoff; median follow-up was 53.0 months. The median OS was 13.2 months (95% CI 12.1-14.5), with 1-, 3-, and 5-year OS of 50.9%, 41.1%, and 36.9%; because patients dying before three qualifying records accumulated could not enter the cohort, these estimates apply to patients meeting the case-identification algorithm and are likely to overstate population survival. OS was markedly longer in women than in men (median 50.9 vs 8.2 months), and longer in patients without cirrhosis recorded at diagnosis than in those with cirrhosis (18.5 vs 9.0 months; both P < 0.001). Hepatitis B was the most frequently recorded specific etiology (29.4%); among mutually exclusive categories, NAFLD-associated HCC had the most favourable survival (5-year OS 61.0%) and alcohol-related HCC the least (median 8.8 months), while HBV-HDV co-infection was associated with longer survival than HBV mono-infection (58.2 vs 12.0 months; P < 0.001), a difference that persisted after adjustment for age, sex, and cirrhosis; no specific etiology could be assigned in 56.1% of patients. Sensitivity analyses restricting etiologic ascertainment to codes recorded within 3 months before to 3 months after diagnosis, or incorporating viral serology, attenuated the survival of the specific viral etiologies, indicating survival-dependent ascertainment. In a multivariable Cox model fitted in the three-month landmark cohort (n = 8958), older age, male sex, cirrhosis, and systemic therapy were associated with higher mortality (all P < 0.001), with time-varying associations for age, cirrhosis, and systemic therapy. The association of local therapy with mortality was not constant over follow-up (HR 0.78, 95% CI 0.72-0.85 during 0-24 months after the landmark and 1.22, 1.04-1.43 thereafter); the overall association was no longer evident after liver transplantation was excluded from the local-therapy category. Care was highly centralised within secondary and tertiary institutions. CONCLUSIONS: In this nationwide analysis, HCC in Turkey was characterised by limited OS and pronounced sex-based disparities, with survival differing by cirrhosis status and recorded etiology; etiologic ascertainment was itself survival-dependent, so these contrasts describe recorded categories. Hepatitis B was the most frequently recorded specific etiology, underscoring the continued importance of HBV prevention, screening, and surveillance, while HCV, HDV, alcohol-related and metabolic liver disease accounted for smaller recorded proportions; temporal trends in etiology were not analysed. Because tumour stage and liver function were unavailable, the treatment-survival associations are descriptive and subject to confounding by indication. Efforts focused on HBV control, earlier detection, risk-based surveillance of patients with cirrhosis, and improved referral pathways may improve population-level outcomes.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: This study investigated relationships between the skeletal muscle index (SMI) and the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME), peripheral immune phenotypes, and serum biomarkers in advanced pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) and evaluated the prognostic significance of these parameters. METHODS: A retrospective analysis of 119 advanced PDAC patients was performed. Sarcopenia was diagnosed using sex-specific SMI cut-offs from baseline L3-level computed tomography (CT) images. The TIME was characterized by multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF; n = 31), peripheral immunity by flow cytometry, and serum biomarkers by routine testing. Associations with SMI were examined using Spearman correlation; prognostic relevance was assessed using Cox proportional hazards models. RESULTS: Sarcopenia (56/119, 47.1%) was associated with shorter progression-free survival (PFS) (8.83 vs. 12.03 months, p = 0.016) and overall survival (OS) (10.20 vs. 17.33 months, p = 0.014). SMI correlated most strongly with stromal CD8+ T cells (ρ = 0.52), stromal total T cells (ρ = 0.52), and stromal M2 macrophages (ρ = 0.50) in the TIME; with circulating Th2-like cells (ρ = -0.58) and CD4+ memory T cells (ρ = 0.45) peripherally; and with hemoglobin (ρ = 0.32) among serum markers. In multivariable Cox regression, stromal CD4+ Treg percentage independently predicted OS (hazard ratio [HR] = 7.60, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.60-36.22, p = 0.011), stromal CD56dim natural killer (NK)-cell density predicted PFS (HR = 1.015, 95% CI 1.001-1.028, p = 0.031), and the lymphocyte-to-monocyte ratio (LMR) predicted both PFS (HR = 0.86, p = 0.023) and OS (HR = 0.83, p = 0.009). No peripheral lymphocyte subset reached prognostic significance. CONCLUSION: SMI is broadly associated with local and systemic immune phenotypes in advanced PDAC. Stromal CD4+ regulatory T cells (Tregs), CD56dim NK cells, and LMR carry independent prognostic information and may complement body-composition assessment.

papers.abstract_en: Non‑small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains a leading cause of cancer‑associated mortality and urgently requires new therapeutic agents. In the present study, phenotypic screening of natural herbal extracts was performed, identifying Disporum cantoniense extract as a selective inhibitor of NSCLC cell viability. Bioactivity‑guided fractionation further revealed that the petroleum ether fraction (DPF) was the major active fraction. DPF suppressed the viability, proliferation, colony formation, migration and invasion of A549 and H1299 cells while exhibiting weaker cytotoxicity toward BEAS‑2B cells. In addition, DPF increased propidium iodide (PI)‑positive cell death and lactate dehydrogenase release in NSCLC cells, indicating that DPF‑induced viability loss was accompanied by membrane‑damaging cytotoxicity. Transcriptomic and network pharmacology analyses indicated significant enrichment of autophagy‑, apoptosis‑, AMPK‑, mTOR‑, and MAPK‑associated pathways. Mechanistically, DPF increased LC3‑II accumulation, promoted green fluorescent protein‑LC3 puncta formation and autophagic flux, and activated the AMPK/mTOR/unc‑51 like autophagy activating kinase 1 and MEK/ERK signaling pathways. DPF also induced apoptosis, as demonstrated by increased Annexin V positivity, elevated cleaved caspase‑3 and Bax expression, reduced Bcl‑2 expression, and reduced cytotoxicity in Bax‑Bak double‑knockout mouse embryonic fibroblast (MEF) cells. Notably, pharmacological inhibition of autophagy or its upstream regulators attenuated DPF‑induced cytotoxicity. In addition, autophagy‑deficient Atg7‑/‑ MEF cells exhibited reduced DPF‑induced PI‑positive cell death, loss of cell viability, and caspase‑3 activation, further supporting the involvement of Atg7‑dependent autophagy in DPF‑induced apoptosis. In a xenograft model, DPF significantly inhibited tumor growth and increased apoptosis‑ and autophagy‑associated markers in tumor tissues without evident systemic toxicity. Collectively, these findings identify DPF as a principal anti‑NSCLC fraction of Disporum cantoniense and suggest that it suppresses NSCLC progression through AMPK/mTOR/unc‑51 like autophagy activating kinase 1‑ and MEK/ERK‑mediated autophagy‑dependent apoptosis.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and peripheral artery disease (PAD) significantly contribute to morbidity and mortality among older adults. The geographic co-occurrence may indicate shared exposures; however, global population-level evidence remains scarce. METHODS: Utilizing Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2021 estimates, the analysis focused on COPD and PAD incidence in adults aged ≥ 70 years across 202 countries and territories. Disease-specific incidence quartiles characterized spatial co-occurrence. Random forest models with SHAP (Shapley Additive Explanations) ranked exposure contributions, while negative binomial regression with population offsets estimated associations and population-attributable fractions (PAFs). A quartile-based composite risk index summarized cumulative exposure. RESULTS: The global median incidence was 1150.16 per 100,000 for COPD and 695.4 per 100,000 for PAD. High-incidence regions exhibited partial geographic overlap. Smoking, high LDL cholesterol, and kidney dysfunction correlated with the incidence of both diseases, whereas several additional exposures were disease-specific. Elevated LDL cholesterol had the largest positive association with COPD incidence (RR 1.149), whereas high sugar-sweetened beverage intake exhibited the largest positive association among PAD-specific exposures (RR 1.059). Model-derived cumulative PAFs were 29.7% for COPD and 23.7% for PAD. CONCLUSION: COPD and PAD demonstrate distinct yet overlapping global spatial patterns among older adults, sharing several population-level exposure correlates. Due to the cross-sectional and ecological nature of this study, the observed associations and PAFs should not be interpreted as individual-level causal effects. These findings may inform regional public health planning and generate hypotheses for prospective validation of integrated cardiopulmonary risk assessment.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Mutations in the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) gene are known to cause cystic fibrosis (CF), a condition that shares several pathophysiological pulmonary features with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Despite these similarities, the relationship between CFTR gene mutations and the risk of developing COPD remains unclear and poorly understood. METHODS: We employed exon sequencing to detect CFTR exon variations in 208 COPD patients and 100 control subjects with normal lung function. Subsequently, we applied the adenine base editor system to generate cells and animal models carrying the CFTR chr7:117227874A>G (I556V) variant. Airway epithelial cell models were used to examine the effect of the I556V variant on reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels and mitochondrial membrane potential. Additionally, conventional I556V-CFTR variant (CFTRV/V ) and wild-type (CFTRI/I ) mice were exposed to either air or 6 months of cigarette smoke. Immune cell counts were obtained from bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) samples. RESULTS: Clinically, we identified seven CFTR variants, with I556V showing a significant association with COPD risk (P = 0.045). Individuals carrying the I556V variant had a 2.12-fold increased risk of developing COPD (OR = 2.12, 95% CI = 1.16-3.86), which increased to 96% after adjusting for age, gender, and smoking status (OR = 1.96, 95% CI = 1.01-3.81). Cells harboring the I556V-CFTR variant exhibited a 27.27% increase in ROS levels and an 85.38% increase in the JC-1 monomer ratio (indicating significant loss of mitochondrial membrane potential) compared to CFTRI/I cells. In mice, the I556V-CFTR variant led to significant impairment of lung function and exacerbated airway remodeling after 6 months of cigarette smoke (CS) exposure, characterized by a 23.03% increase in airway wall thickness and a 48.40% increase in collagen deposition compared to CS-exposed CFTRI/I mice. Moreover, there was exacerbated lung inflammation in I556V-CFTR variant mice compared to CFTRI/I . CONCLUSION: In conclusion, the I556V-CFTR variant is a risk factor for COPD. It likely contributes to disease pathogenesis by downregulating CFTR expression, thereby exacerbating oxidative stress and inflammatory responses.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Ongoing efforts in minimally invasive surgery aim to reduce access sites. This study evaluated the feasibility of the da Vinci SP platform for single-site plus one-port robotic distal pancreatectomy (SSRDP) by comparing perioperative outcomes with a previously reported Xi-based approach. METHODS: Patients who underwent SSRDP using the SP or Xi at two tertiary centres from February 2015 to September 2023 were retrospectively reviewed. Each centre exclusively used one platform. RESULTS: Thirty-two patients underwent SSRDP (SP, n = 20; Xi, n = 12). The SP group had higher age, body mass index, and ASA scores. Operative time was shorter in the SP group, whereas blood loss, spleen preservation, conversion, postoperative pancreatic fistula, and overall complications were comparable. CONCLUSIONS: In this early multicenter experience, SSRDP using the SP platform was feasible and achieved acceptable perioperative outcomes comparable to those of Xi-SSRDP.

papers.abstract_en: Accurate assessment of different types of prostate cancer (PCa) lesions is a crucial part of treatment planning. Following a computed tomography (CT) or a positron emission tomography (PET)/CT imaging scan, a significant amount of time is required from the clinicians to detect lesions and characterize them by their anatomical locations. To facilitate the development of new image analysis applications, we investigated the potential of automated classification of PCa lesions between bone metastases, lymph node metastases, local lesions, and other PCa lesions in CT images via machine learning (ML) and deep learning models. We annotated a total of 4949 PCa lesions by their type in a private dataset of   18  F-prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) PET/CT images of 532 PCa patients and an external test set of publicly available PSMA PET/CT images from 30 patients. Using information of coordinates of the detected lesions, we automatically extracted 15 different features from the CT and the results of the automated 3D anatomical segmentation tool TotalSegmentator for each lesion, and trained several traditional ML models to classify lesions by their anatomical type. Additionally, we experimented with convolutional neural networks (CNNs) of different dimensionalities with CT and TotalSegmentator inputs. According to our results, the most accurate model was XGBoost with an overall accuracy of 96.0%. It identified bone metastases, lymph node metastases, and local lesions with sensitivities of 97.9±1.2%, 95.2±1.3%, and 93.1±2.8% in the five-fold cross-validation experiments of the primary data and 96.3%, 94.0%, and 80.0% on the external test set, respectively. Conversely, the CNNs underperformed the best ML models in distinguishing local lesions. To conclude, a simple ML model can accurately classify PCa lesions between bone, lymph node, and local lesions based on CT images, lesion locations, and automated anatomical segmentation data, but more research is required for distinguishing PCa lesions outside these categories.

papers.abstract_en: To develop and validate a combined model for detecting pituitary microadenomas in suspected cases using non-contrast T1-weighted sagittal (T1SAG) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and to assess its performance as a non-contrast imaging-based tool for clinical decision support.This retrospective two-center study enrolled 519 patients with suspected pituitary microadenomas, divided into a training set (n = 321), an internal validation set (n = 80), and an external test set (n = 118). papers.abstract_en: Studies applying artificial intelligence (AI) to tuberculosis (TB) detection from chest radiographs (CXR) focus on models and metrics, yet the quality, provenance and reproducibility of the data workflow decide the reliability of results; duplicate images and non-patient-level splitting inflate evaluation metrics. We propose a seven-step data-governance workflow: multi-source standardisation, provenance management, three-hash deduplication (MD5, pHash, dHash), patient-level splitting, invariant-check auditing, lung segmentation and version freezing by data fingerprint. Four leakage scenarios (deduplication on or off; patient-level or random split) were repeated 20 times with paired splits and compared with the clean scenario on per-repeat differences. On 46,410 CXR images from seven public sources, the workflow removed duplicates at file and content level, standardised 16,554 TB Portals DICOM images, generated 34,554 lung masks without failure and sealed every layer with SHA-256 hashes. On the three-class multi-source corpus, the area under the curve (AUC) saturated near 0.997 in every scenario, consistent with source-class confounding; paired leakage effects were statistically detectable but below 0.1 percentage points. On a single-source probe task (drug resistance within TB Portals), random image-level splitting inflated the internal AUC by 1.7 percentage points (95% confidence interval 0.9 to 2.4; p = 0.001), or 1.2 points after a deduplication gap found during revision was repaired; in a holdout design, an internal gap of 1.1 points shrank to 0.4 points on a patient-disjoint holdout. The magnitude of leakage depends on data structure and must be measured; a rigorous governance workflow makes that measurement, and data reuse, verifiable.

papers.abstract_en: Accurate characterisation of the wound bed, the relative proportions of granulation, slough and necrotic tissue described by the red-yellow-black model, is central to monitoring healing and guiding debridement in chronic-wound care, yet in routine practice, it is judged visually and is poorly reproducible between clinicians. We investigated automatic, pixel-level segmentation of these three classes within the wound region of interest. A corpus of 404 photographs was curated from a public wound image collection and densely annotated by wound care clinicians with a purpose-built, cluster-assisted labelling tool. Five deep learning architectures spanning convolutional, transformer, hybrid and ensemble families were trained on one frozen data split under a largely shared pipeline, with limited, fully documented architecture-specific tuning, and scored on a shared 62-image test set. The models fell within a narrow mean intersection-over-union band (0.748-0.818). The strongest single model, a purely convolutional network, was statistically indistinguishable from the best ensemble, and simply averaging already-trained convolutional and transformer models matched that ensemble at no additional training cost. Slough remained consistently the hardest tissue. Translated into clinical units, per-wound tissue percentages were recovered with small mean bias (within ± 5 percentage points) but wide single-image limits of agreement (about ± 25-50 percentage points), so the measurement suits aggregate and longitudinal assessment rather than single-image reading. Within this dataset, split and training protocol, the choice among the strong hierarchical architectures was not decisive: a single strong model is the pragmatic option for clinical deployment, with an ensemble reserved for maximal accuracy and class balance.

papers.abstract_en: HLA-A*02:01-restricted PB1413+CD8+ T cells provide the broadest reported cross-reactive immunity against influenza A, B, and C viruses. Here, we investigated T cell receptor (TCR) clonotypic signatures within these universal A2/PB1413+CD8+ T cell pools, compared with immunodominant influenza A-specific M158+CD8+ T cells and codominant influenza B-specific A2/HA543+CD8+ memory T cells. Using single-cell reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction and RNA sequencing methodologies, we defined TCRαβ repertoire composition and diversity. Our study shows that CD8+ T cells responding to these 3 epitopes differ in magnitude and TCRαβ repertoires in terms of gene usage and sharing, underpinned by specific TCR and structural features for each pMHC-I specificity. Our data demonstrated that the A2/PB1413+CD8+ TCRαβ repertoire encompassed diverse gene segment usage within both TCRα and TCRβ chains. These were, however, greatly variable across HLA-A2*02:01-expressing individuals and lacked any shared features within TRAV, TRBV, TRBJ, and TRAJ gene segments. This A2/PB1413+CD8+ TCRαβ diversity stemmed from the low probability of recombination attributed to a large number of N-insertions in the TCRβ chain. PB1413+CD8+ T cells also displayed remarkable plasticity in recognition of the A2/PB1413 epitope depicted by versatile CD8+ T cell recognition patterns of the universal A2/PB1413 epitope across HLA-A*02:01-expressing individuals. Conversely, TCRαβ repertoires within A2/BHA543+CD8+ and M158+CD8+ T cells displayed common TRAV, TRBV, TRBJ, and TRAJ gene segments, shared across HLA-A*02:01-expressing individuals and recognizing key residues within A2/BHA543 and A2/M158 epitopes. Overall, our data showed a great level of TCRαβ gene usage diversity within universal A2/PB1413+CD8+ T cells, indicating that the TCRαβ clonal plasticity defines universal immunity toward human influenza viruses.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: This study aimed to evaluate the impact of pathological changes in bile duct cysts on the clinical and liver pathological findings in early infantile patients with congenital biliary dilatation (CBD). METHOD: In patients with CBD who underwent definitive surgery ≤ 4 months of age, the clinical and liver pathological findings were analyzed according to the presence or absence of inflammatory and fibrotic changes on the luminal side of the bile duct cyst. RESULTS: Among the 14 patients with infantile CBD, 8 had inflammatory cell infiltration (iCBD), and 4 of these 8 patients showed the formation of a collagen layer together. In the remaining six patients, no infiltration of inflammatory cells or formation of collagen layers was observed (non-iCBD). In the iCBD group, the preoperative liver biochemistry levels were higher, the cyst amylase levels were lower, and the degree of liver fibrosis was more severe than those in the non-iCBD group, with significant differences. In comparisons of iCBD patients, there were no differences in the preoperative liver biochemistry levels, cyst amylase levels, and severity of liver fibrosis between the presence and absence of a collagen layer. CONCLUSION: Inflammatory and fibrotic changes in the bile duct cysts due to obstructive cholestasis may affect the clinical and liver histopathological differences in early infantile CBD after birth.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Building on our previous work demonstrating that balloon-retained gastro-jejunostomy tubes (BGJ) avoid complications unique to disc-retained devices but require more frequent replacement, we evaluated caregiver experience and healthcare resource use to better inform tube selection in children. METHODS: Families whose children had experienced both Freka® percutaneous endoscopic gastro-jejunostomy (FPEGJ) and BGJ completed a paired questionnaire assessing nine experience domains (0-5 Likert-type scales) with free-text comments. Scores were compared using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test and comments underwent thematic analysis. A 24-month NHS resource-use model compared staged FPEGJ followed by planned BGJ conversion with primary laparoscopic BGJ insertion using 2026/27 NHS Payment Scheme tariffs. RESULTS: Twelve of thirteen eligible families responded(92.3%). Nine(75%) preferred BGJ and three had no preference. No questionnaire domain differed significantly, although BGJ showed trends towards greater comfort and easier daily care, while FPEGJ showed a trend towards less leakage. Families favoured BGJ because of its lower profile, avoidance of general anaesthesia (GA) for replacement and avoidance of buried bumper syndrome. Standard staged FPEGJ treatment cost £4,192 over 24 months compared with £6,024 for primary laparoscopic BGJ, saving £1,831(30.4%). Even with laparoscopic assistance, FPEGJ remained 22.1% less expensive. Routine BGJ exchanges were the principal cost driver. CONCLUSIONS: A staged FPEGJ-to-BGJ strategy appears to provide the best balance between caregiver experience and NHS resource use. However, disc-retained devices commit children to at least one future GA, the associated burden of which is not fully captured by cost analysis. BGJ with reliable 12-month durability may further reduce procedural burden and healthcare costs.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Lung ultrasound and targeted echocardiography let the neonatal team examine lungs and heart at the cot side, but neither shows the airway. Flexible bronchoscopy does, and it is increasingly performed inside the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU). METHODS: Narrative review of published series of flexible bronchoscopy in infants cared for in neonatal units, supported by pediatric intensive care studies and society standards. Certainty of evidence was not graded. RESULTS: Twelve neonatal series (652 infants) were identified; all but one were single-center and most were retrospective. In referred infants, airway abnormalities were reported in 60-96% and a change in management in 63-94%; when intubated neonates were examined routinely, significant airway disease was found in 19%. The main indications were repeated extubation failure, persistent atelectasis, stridor and suspected congenital anomaly. Transient desaturation occurred in 2-24% of procedures, and one bilateral pneumothorax was reported. Where identified, the operator was usually a pediatric pulmonologist, so the procedure is currently a bedside consultation, not point-of-care testing in the sense applied to ultrasound. No study has examined mortality, bronchopulmonary dysplasia, duration of ventilation or length of stay. CONCLUSIONS: Bedside flexible bronchoscopy answers questions about the neonatal airway that ultrasound cannot, and in selected infants it often changes what is done next. Its place should be defined by prospective studies with stated denominators, consistent reporting of physiological cost, and a training pathway for neonatal operators. Reduced exposure to tuberculosis and other hospital pathogens by avoiding transport is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated benefit.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: There is limited evidence to guide implementation of recommended collaborative palliative care (PC) models for hospitalized patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). We sought to characterize palliative needs and identify barriers to PC delivery to inform inpatient collaborative care models. METHODS: We conducted a sequential explanatory mixed-methods study of hospitalized adults with COPD and physicians (hospitalists and pulmonologists) at two urban teaching hospitals in the United States. Patients rated their palliative needs in a survey, followed by a semi-structured interview. Physicians rated the perceived needs of a typical hospitalized patient with moderate-to-severe COPD, and then a purposive sample completed an interview. Survey data were summarized descriptively. Two independent coders conducted content analysis of interview transcripts to identify convergent and divergent perspectives across participant groups. RESULTS: Fifteen patients (mean age 67 years; 47% female, 47% Black, 47% White) and 39 physicians (56% hospitalists, 44% pulmonologists, 44% female, 64% White, 23% Asian) completed surveys. All patients and 15 physicians completed interviews. Participants identified three domains of palliative needs: physical symptoms, psychosocial and emotional distress, and communication. Although physicians rated palliative needs as more burdensome than patients did, they frequently deferred addressing these needs due to competing clinical demands, prognostic uncertainty, and the perceived limited value of inpatient PC consultation. Patients reported that their palliative needs often remained unaddressed. CONCLUSIONS: Collaborative inpatient PC models for COPD should prioritize addressing common palliative needs, strengthen generalist PC skills, establish clear criteria for specialist PC involvement, and improve coordination across care settings.

papers.abstract_en: Asthma is a common chronic inflammatory airway disease. Plasminogen activator inhibitor 1 (PAI-1) contributes to airway inflammation, remodelling, disease severity, and exacerbations. As anthocyanins (ACN) possess antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, and oxidative stress is a key feature of asthma, investigating the efficacy of anthocyanin supplementation in this population is warranted. Although the study was originally designed to assess variability to plan a larger study in the event only five participants were recruited. The study design was a cross-over design. Participants received either a 300 mg ACN supplement or an identical placebo for eight weeks. Feasibility outcomes and asthma symptom control were assessed, alongside exploratory analyses of inflammatory markers, including fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO) and salivary plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 (PAI-1). Associations between changes in PAI-1, Dietary Inflammatory Index (DII) scores, and the PAI-1 4G/5G polymorphism were also explored. Improvements in asthma symptom control were observed following ACN supplementation, including reduced daytime and nighttime symptoms and no activity limitation, similar to the placebo phase. Moreover, an absence of short-acting beta-agonist (SABA) reliever use N/N 0/5, 0%; SABA use reappeared during the placebo phase N/N 1/5, 20%. Preliminary findings support the feasibility of conducting a larger trial of ACN supplementation in adults with asthma. While ACN supplementation may have a positive effect on asthma symptom control, the findings are exploratory and require confirmation in adequately powered studies with larger sample sizes.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Financial toxicity (FT) refers to the direct and indirect consequences of cancer diagnosis and treatment and is a key mediator of quality of life (QOL) and survival in cancer patients. To address this, financial navigation (FN) programs have been implemented in many cancer centers. At our large tertiary care cancer center, the FN program uses the Comprehensive Score for Financial Toxicity (COST) to screen patients undergoing first cancer treatment. We aimed to better understand FT, risk factors, and association with outcomes in our cancer population. METHODS: We identified 1906 patients with any cancer diagnosis and a completed COST between 6/2021 and 2/2024. Sociodemographic data including the Area Deprivation Index (ADI), disease, and treatment characteristics as well as patient-reported outcomes (PROMIS10, PHQ9 and NCCN DT) were collected. Risk factors for FT and association of FT on overall survival (OS) were analyzed. RESULTS: Median age was 65 years (IQR 56-72); 54% female, 82% white, 57% married, 47% insured privately, and 35% with Medicare. Younger age, race/ethnicity, insurance type, tobacco use, and higher ADI were associated with higher FT. Higher distress (NCCN DT, N = 1001) and lower physical (N = 1474) and mental (N = 1505) health (PROMIS10) were also associated with higher FT. FT was not associated with time to treat (TTT) or OS. However, higher ADI was significantly associated with TTT (HR 0.98, 95% CI 0.96-1.00, p = 0.04) but not OS. CONCLUSIONS: Our study provides insights into risk factors for FT in a large cancer population. We did not demonstrate a significant association of FT on survival. Further analysis in specific disease groups is needed to better understand these relationships.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Sleep disturbance is prevalent among adults with cancer and often co-occurs with multiple physical and psychological symptoms. Although resilience has been associated with better sleep outcomes, evidence integrating overall symptom burden and resilience remains limited. OBJECTIVE: To identify factors associated with sleep quality in adults with cancer, focusing on co-occurring symptom burden and resilience. METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 159 adults with cancer recruited from a tertiary hospital and online patient communities in the Republic of Korea. Sleep quality was assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index. Symptom burden was measured with the Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System 29-Item Profile, and resilience with the Korean version of the Connor-Davidson Resilience Scale. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with poor sleep quality, and hierarchical multiple linear regression examined factors associated with sleep quality scores. RESULTS: The mean sleep quality score was 6.99 ± 3.84, and 42.1% of participants were classified as poor sleepers. Being 1-3 years postdiagnosis and having received radiotherapy were independently associated with higher odds of poor sleep. Higher mental health summary scores and higher resilience were associated with lower odds of poor sleep after adjustment for sociodemographic and clinical factors. The final regression model explained 34.1% of the variance in sleep quality. CONCLUSIONS: Poor sleep was common among adults with cancer. Mental health and resilience were independently associated with sleep quality beyond clinical characteristics. These findings highlight the relevance of considering psychosocial factors alongside clinical characteristics when assessing sleep problems in supportive oncology care.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Biomarkers associated with first-line chemoimmunotherapy outcomes in HER2-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remain incompletely characterized. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether TP53 truncating mutations are associated with clinical outcomes after first-line pembrolizumab plus pemetrexed-platinum in patients with HER2-mutant NSCLC. PATIENTS AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective clinicogenomic study using the nationwide Center for Cancer Genomics and Advanced Therapeutics (C-CAT) database. Patients with advanced or recurrent HER2-mutant NSCLC who received first-line pembrolizumab plus pemetrexed-platinum were included. The primary endpoint was time to treatment failure (TTF). RESULTS: Among 69 patients, 21 (30.4%) harbored TP53 truncating mutations. Patients with TP53 truncating mutations had shorter TTF than those without TP53 truncating mutations (median, 6.0 versus 7.6 months; hazard ratio [HR], 1.97; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.11-3.49; log-rank P = 0.018). The 9-month TTF rates were 4.8% and 40.6%, respectively. After adjustment for age, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status, and programmed death-ligand 1 tumor proportion score, TP53 truncating mutations remained associated with shorter TTF (HR, 1.98; 95% CI 1.08-3.63; P = 0.026). No significant differences were observed in overall survival or objective response rate. CONCLUSIONS: TP53 truncating mutations were associated with shorter TTF during first-line pembrolizumab plus pemetrexed-platinum in HER2-mutant NSCLC, without significant differences in overall survival or objective response rate. These findings suggest a potential association with shorter treatment durability and require validation in independent cohorts.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Primary pulmonary osteosarcoma (PPOS) is an exceptionally rare malignant tumor that arises within the lung parenchyma. Fewer than 40 cases of PPOS have been reported to date. Owing to its rarity, the clinical features and prognostic factors of PPOS remain poorly defined. OBJECTIVE: To report a new case of PPOS and perform a pooled retrospective analysis of published cases to identify clinical profiles and potential prognostic determinants. METHODS: A comprehensive literature review was conducted using the PubMed, Medline, and Cochrane Library databases. Thirty-eight reported cases of PPOS were identified. Among these, sufficient clinical and survival data of 25 patients, including one from our institution, were available for analysis. Overall survival (OS) was assessed using the Kaplan-Meier method and Cox proportional hazards models. RESULTS: The median age of the pooled cohort was 64 years. Kaplan-Meier and multivariable Cox analyses demonstrated that older age (> 64 years) was associated with poorer OS and that surgical resection significantly improved survival. Among surgical patients, adjuvant chemotherapy was associated with a trend toward prolonged OS, although the difference was not statistically significant (P = 0.053). Age-stratified analysis revealed a survival benefit of surgery in both the ≤ 64-year age group and the > 64-year age group (P = 0.003 and P < 0.001, respectively), and no significant difference in OS was observed according to tumor size among surgically treated patients (P = 0.89). CONCLUSION: PPOS is an aggressive malignancy with poor prognosis. Age and surgical resection were found to be crucial prognostic factors. A combination of surgery and chemotherapy may offer additional survival benefits to selected patients. Given that the benefits of surgery were observed across all age groups and that no difference in survival was observed according to tumor size among surgically treated patients, advanced age and larger tumor size alone should not preclude consideration of surgical intervention in patients with adequate performance status. Larger multi-institutional studies are needed to validate these findings.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Accurate intraoperative identification of the tumor-brain interface is important in brain metastasis surgery, but visual assessment under white light is subjective. Narrow-band imaging (NBI) enhances hemoglobin-dependent optical contrast without an exogenous agent; whether its intraoperative appearance corresponds to tumor tissue, and whether it measurably increases tumor-to-normal image contrast, has not been established in this setting. METHODS: In this retrospective, single-center, exploratory study, we evaluated 25 consecutive patients with brain metastases resected using a 4K three-dimensional exoscope equipped with NBI. In three selected patients, spatially adjacent specimens were separately sampled from grayish-appearing and whitish-appearing regions and assessed histopathologically in a non-blinded, descriptive manner. In all 25 patients, paired white-light and NBI images were retrospectively analyzed in Fiji/ImageJ using regions of interest drawn over tissue visually judged to be tumor or normal brain. RESULTS: In the three patients with paired histology, grayish-appearing specimens contained metastatic tumor cells and whitish-appearing specimens did not; this observation derives from a small, selectively sampled subset and should be regarded as preliminary. Across all 25 patients, absolute tumor-to-normal gray-value contrast was significantly greater under NBI than white light (69.628 ± 45.338 vs. 44.287 ± 29.640; mean paired increase, 25.342; 95% CI, 9.169-41.514; p = 0.0035; Cohen's dz = 0.647), although this increase was not observed in all patients. CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory, non-blinded, retrospective study, NBI increased objective image contrast between visually identified tumor and normal brain relative to white light, and its grayish appearance corresponded to tumor tissue in a small histologically sampled subset. These findings support NBI as a feasible, agent-free adjunct that warrants prospective, blinded validation before its diagnostic accuracy or clinical benefit can be assessed.

papers.abstract_en: Background/Objectives: AP-2 transcription factors are increasingly recognized as key regulators in cancer biology. The TFAP2E gene, which encodes the AP-2ε transcription factor, remains understudied in cancer compared with other AP-2 family members. The scarcity of studies examining potential AP-2ε targets and related genes limits our understanding of its functional significance. Moreover, related studies have not incorporated a screening step to select the tumor type for justified molecular investigation. Through comparison of tumor-normal expression differences in a pan-cancer spectrum, this study prioritized ovarian serous carcinoma for downstream assessment. Methods: Expression patterns were evaluated using GENT2, GEPIA2, and TNMplot. After prioritizing ovarian serous carcinoma, TFAP2E and related signatures in TCGA-OV were analyzed using transcriptomic and clinical data from GDC and CDR, followed by comparison of findings with the GSE32062 cohort. The workflow included survival and clinicopathological analyses, outcome-independent limma-voom differential expression analysis and WGCNA, MCODE clustering, gene ontology, immune subtype and stemness assessment, PCA, CancerHallmarks enrichment, clinically adjusted Cox and competing-risk survival modeling, and HPA-derived immunostaining evaluation. Additional analyses assessed WGCNA parameter stability and preservation in GSE32062, an outcome-independent MAD-based variability screen, AP-2 family coexpression, and promoter motif enrichment. Results:TFAP2E was downregulated in ovarian cancer across the three queried resources, whereas higher expression was associated with favorable survival across multiple endpoints. Differential expression and WGCNA identified a TFAP2E-associated signature; its ontology indicated GPCR, stimulus responsiveness, and KRAS enrichment for the 933-gene module. The WGCNA pink module was stable across alternative settings, moderately preserved in GSE32062 (Zsummary = 7.86), and enriched in the outcome-independent MAD screening. GSE32062 supported concordant gene expression patterns and showed an association of TFAP2E with progression-free survival. Exploratory immune analyses showed a modestly increased proportion of C5 tumors in the higher-expression groups, whereas differences in stemness were statistically insignificant. The TFAP2E group associations with PFI and DSS in TCGA-OV and with PFS in GSE32062 remained significant after clinical adjustment; Fine-Gray sensitivity analyses gave consistent results for DSS. Immunohistochemistry provided protein-level characterization; eighteen entries differed between representative normal and tumor specimens, with lower tumor staining in fifteen. The seven-gene candidate set showed a clinically adjusted DSS association in TCGA-OV, which was not supported in the GSE32062 evaluation model. Conclusions:TFAP2E expression is associated with survival and a transcriptomic cross-cohort pattern in ovarian serous carcinoma. Covariate-adjusted and competing-risk analyses supported the association but did not establish clinical utility. The highlighted genes remain exploratory candidates for mechanistic investigation.

papers.abstract_en: Background/Objectives: Giant congenital melanocytic nevus (GCMN) is a rare developmental disorder arising from abnormal proliferation and differentiation of neural crest-derived melanocytes. It poses substantial clinical challenges due to cosmetic disfigurement, malignant potential, and the limited efficacy of current treatments. This study aimed to investigate the therapeutic effects and underlying molecular mechanisms of tunlametinib (HL-085), a novel selective MEK1/2 inhibitor, in GCMN. Methods: Primary GCMN cells and human GCMN explants were isolated, cultured, and validated to establish in vitro cellular and explant models. Following tunlametinib treatment, global transcriptional changes were analyzed using bulk RNA sequencing. Melanogenesis was assessed via Fontana-Masson staining, Western blotting, and immunofluorescence. Cell viability, apoptosis, and cell cycle distribution were evaluated using the CCK-8 assay, flow cytometry, TUNEL staining, and Western blotting for apoptosis- and cell cycle-related proteins. Results: Tunlametinib treatment significantly suppressed melanogenesis in GCMN cells and explant tissues at the phenotypic, histological, and protein levels, and reduced cell viability in a concentration-dependent manner. Transcriptomic analysis revealed marked alterations in gene expression profiles following treatment, with prominent changes in apoptosis- and cell cycle-related genes. Subsequent cellular assays and tissue staining confirmed that tunlametinib significantly increased early apoptosis and induced G1/S cell cycle arrest. Conclusions: Collectively, our findings demonstrate that tunlametinib inhibits proliferation and melanin production in GCMN cells by modulating the RAS-ERK pathway, providing a theoretical basis for its use as a targeted therapeutic strategy for GCMN.

papers.abstract_en: Sarcopenia, low muscle mass, and low muscle radiodensity are increasingly being considered factors associated with treatment outcomes in patients with gynecological malignancies. Despite the growing body of evidence, body composition assessment is not routinely incorporated into clinical practice. The aim of this review was to present current evidence on the associations of muscle parameters with survival, complications, systemic treatment toxicity, and quality of life, as well as to discuss the opportunities and limitations of computed tomography (CT) and bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA) in body composition monitoring. A narrative literature review was conducted using the PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science databases, primarily covering publications from 2019 to 2026, together with earlier studies relevant to the topic. Systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and selected observational, longitudinal, and interventional studies were included. The available evidence indicates that low muscle mass and low muscle radiodensity are primarily associated with poorer overall survival and an increased risk of selected postoperative complications. Evidence regarding progression-free survival, disease recurrence, chemotherapy toxicity, and quality of life remains less consistent. Low muscle mass may occur independently of body weight and body mass index (BMI); therefore, routine anthropometric assessment may fail to identify adverse changes in body composition. CT image analysis enables quantitative assessment of muscle mass and evaluation of muscle radiodensity, whereas BIA may serve as a complementary tool for repeated body composition monitoring. However, its use is limited by the effects of hydration status, edema, and ascites, as well as by the lack of validated cut-off values for patients with gynecological malignancies. Body composition assessment should be interpreted in conjunction with evaluations of muscle strength, physical performance, nutritional status, treatment toxicity, and quality of life. Prospective studies are needed to determine whether body composition monitoring and the implementation of targeted supportive care improve treatment tolerance and clinical outcomes.

papers.abstract_en: Background/Objectives: Prognoses for patients with clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) are associated with complex interactions between tumor and patient characteristics. This cross-sectional study investigated associations between body composition and tumor proteomics and their interaction with survival among patients with ccRCC. Methods: Data from 178 patients in the TCGA-KIRC project were analyzed to assess adipose and skeletal muscle tissue areas at the third lumbar vertebra of diagnostic computed tomography scan images. Patients were classified into four body composition types: high muscle with low adiposity; high muscle with high adiposity; low muscle with low adiposity; and low muscle with high adiposity. Proteins with differential expression (p < 0.05) were screened for interactions with body composition type on survival. Linear regression was used to assess associations, and Cox regression models-adjusted for age, tumor stage, sex, race, and ethnicity-were utilized for survival analysis. Results: Patients with low muscle with low adiposity exhibited worse survival than those having high muscle with high adiposity (hazard ratio, 3.74 [95% CI, 1.69-8.27]). Low muscle with low adiposity was also associated with increased expression of P-cadherin and decreased expression of DIRAS3 (p < 0.05; false discovery rate-corrected p < 0.1), both associated with poor survival in the entire TCGA-KIRC cohort. Among patients having low muscle with high adiposity, high (vs. low) PREX1 expression was associated with 15.8-fold (95% CI, 3.08-80.78) increased mortality. Conclusions: Body composition is associated with differential protein expressions and survival in ccRCC. Therefore, body composition and its associated tumor proteomics may serve as prognostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets in ccRCC.

papers.abstract_en: Background/Objectives: Our previous study identified ZBTB1 as a novel tumor suppressor in estrogen receptor-positive (ER+) breast cancer. Moreover, The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) data analysis showed a much lower level of ZBTB1 in triple-negative breast cancer than in ER+ breast cancer. Triple negative breast cancer (TNBC) lacks effective targeted therapies and largely depends on chemotherapy, while chemotherapy resistance remains a major clinical challenge. This study aimed to explore the role of ZBTB1 in TNBC progression and chemotherapy resistance. Methods: We performed clinical survival analysis, in vitro and in vivo functional experiments, mass spectrometry screening, and mechanistic validation in TNBC and Adriamycin-resistant TNBC cells. Results: We found that ZBTB1 protein is downregulated in TNBC and this downregulation correlates with shorter patient survival. ZBTB1 regulates glycolysis and chemotherapy resistance in TNBC cells. Mechanistically, ZBTB1 interacts with c-Myc and suppresses its transcriptional activity in MDA-MB-231 and MDA-MB-453 but not in Adriamycin-resistant cells (MDA-MB-231/ADR and MDA-MB-453/ADR). LncRNA SAP30L-AS1 is required for maintaining the ZBTB1-c-Myc interaction in TNBC cells. SAP30L-AS1 is significantly depleted in Adriamycin-resistant cells, which disrupts the binding between ZBTB1 and c-Myc. Functional validation revealed that SAP30L-AS1 modulates glycolysis and chemotherapy resistance in TNBC cells in a ZBTB1-dependent manner. Conclusions: Collectively, our data indicate the key role of ZBTB1 in TNBC and ZBTB1 may serve as a novel approach for TNBC treatments.

papers.abstract_en: Background: Compared to chest X-ray, computed tomography (CT) imaging of the chest is more sensitive and specific for identifying pulmonary abnormalities. However, patients with acute leukemia routinely undergo chest X-ray before beginning chemotherapy, and the benefit of obtaining baseline chest CT remains unclear. Methods: In this retrospective study, 50 patients with newly diagnosed acute leukemia who underwent chest X-ray and chest CT without contrast before beginning induction chemotherapy were included. CT imaging reports were independently evaluated by two hematologist-oncologists for infection concern and actionability, and these assessments were compared to the actions taken by the treating physicians. Results: Regardless of the presence of chest X-ray abnormalities, chest CT identified abnormalities in 94% of patients (47/50), a significantly higher detection rate than that for chest X-ray, which demonstrated abnormalities in only 66% of patients (33/50) (p < 0.001). Of the 17 patients with normal chest X-ray findings, 14 (82%) had abnormal chest CT findings. Of these 14 patients, 10 had actionable abnormalities, and four had non-clinically significant findings. All 33 patients with abnormal chest X-ray findings also had abnormal chest CT findings, and three patients with normal chest X-ray findings also had normal chest CT findings. Of the 30 patients with normal or minimal chest X-ray findings compared to chest CT findings, 26 patients (87%) had chest CT findings that were actionable, prompting more aggressive care and/or closer monitoring. On multivariate analysis, patients with both abnormal chest X-ray and chest CT findings had worse overall survival than patients without both abnormal chest X-ray and chest CT findings (p = 0.005). Conclusions: These findings highlight a diagnostic gap, potentially supporting prospective studies on routine chest CT imaging for patients with newly diagnosed acute leukemia.

papers.abstract_en: Introduction: Epidemiological trends indicate that the global colorectal cancer (CRC) mortality will surpass 2.2 million deaths annually by the year 2050; therefore, the identification of novel circulating indicators that may support CRC diagnosis remains an important area of research. Objectives: The diagnostic relevance of circulating chemokines in CRC remains insufficiently understood. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic potential of selected serum C-X-C motif chemokines, CXCL13, CXCL14, and CXCL16, and to compare their diagnostic utility with CEA. Patients and Methods: This study included 62 individuals: 42 patients with CRC and 20 healthy volunteers. Serum chemokines levels were measured using a multiplex bead-based immunoassay (Luminex), and CEA levels via chemiluminescent microparticle immunoassay (CMIA). Results: Significant differences between patients with CRC and healthy controls were observed for serum CXCL13 concentrations. Spearman's analysis revealed a significant negative correlation between CXCL13 and CXCL14. CXCL14 showed the highest diagnostic sensitivity among the chemokines, similar to CEA, while combining CXCL13 or CXCL14 with CEA further increased sensitivity. CXCL13 showed the highest positive predictive value (PPV) among all tested proteins, while its negative predictive value (NPV) and diagnostic accuracy (ACC) exceeded those of CXCL14 and CXCL16. CXCL13 demonstrated the highest AUC among the investigated chemokines and remained independently associated with CRC status in multivariable analysis. CXCL13 combined with CEA yielded the numerically highest overall AUC, although the improvement over CEA alone was not statistically significant. Conclusions: CXCL13 serves as a valuable complementary biomarker, providing crucial additive insights that might augment diagnostic frameworks of patients with CRC. These findings support further evaluation of chemokines as potential adjuncts to established diagnostic biomarkers in larger, independent screening-like study cohorts.

papers.abstract_en: Objective: T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (T-ALL) is a highly aggressive hematological malignancy with poor overall prognosis. This study systematically evaluates the anti-leukemic therapeutic potential and underlying redox-driven mechanisms of PZ2, a novel organic arsenic compound, in T-ALL. Methods: The cytotoxicity of PZ2 against T-ALL cell lines and normal cells was assessed to determine its therapeutic window. RNA-seq was utilized to map transcriptomic alterations. Intracellular redox homeostasis, mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP), cell cycle, and apoptosis were evaluated using flow cytometry and fluorescence microscopy. Ultrastructural changes and key protein expressions were analyzed via TEM, RT-qPCR, and immunoblotting. In vivo efficacy was validated using a T-ALL cell-line-derived xenograft (CDX) mouse model. Results: PZ2 exhibited superior cytotoxicity and an improved safety profile compared to inorganic arsenic trioxide (ATO). Transcriptomic data indicated strong enrichment in apoptosis and autophagy-lysosome pathways. PZ2 induced profound mitochondrial oxidative stress, leading to ROS accumulation, MMP loss, and subsequent activation of caspase-dependent apoptosis-effects that were completely rescued by ROS scavengers. Furthermore, PZ2 triggered G2/M phase arrest and activated autophagic flux (upregulated GABARAPL1 and LC3-II, degraded p62). Notably, pharmacological inhibition of autophagy rescued PZ2-induced apoptosis, revealing a pro-death autophagic mechanism. In vivo, PZ2 significantly suppressed tumor growth and prolonged survival without overt systemic toxicity. Conclusions: PZ2 exhibits potent anti-T-ALL activity that may involve a dual mechanism: ROS-dependent mitochondrial apoptosis and pro-death autophagy potentially associated with GABARAPL1. This novel organic arsenical may represent a promising and potentially safer alternative for leukemia therapy, and these findings suggest a potential interplay between oxidative stress and autophagic cell death.

papers.abstract_en: Background/Objectives: We evaluated the efficacy and safety of first-line treatment with a programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) inhibitor plus platinum-based chemotherapy versus chemotherapy alone in patients aged ≥75 years with extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC). Results: A total of 364 consecutive patients were enrolled. After excluding 21 patients who did not receive treatment or had ineligible histological types, 343 patients were included in the analysis. Of these, 132 were aged ≥75. Compared with chemotherapy alone, administering a PD-L1 inhibitor with chemotherapy significantly improved the median overall survival among elderly patients (13.6 vs. 8.4 months; hazard ratio, 0.543; p = 0.0277). The median progression-free and overall survivals were similar between the ≥75-year and <75-year groups treated with PD-L1 inhibitor plus chemotherapy (4.9 vs. 4.8 months; p = 0.7611 and 13.6 vs. 15 months; p = 0.732, respectively). Immune-related adverse events (irAE) of ≥grade 3 occurred in 4 and 12 patients (p = 0.7823), and non irAE of ≥grade 3 occurred in 47 and 103 patients (p = 0.5247) in the ≥75-years and <75-years subgroups, respectively. Conclusions: In this retrospective study, among patients aged ≥75 years with ES-SCLC, the addition of a PD-L1 inhibitor to platinum-based chemotherapy was associated with longer overall survival. Progression-free and overall survival outcomes were comparable between elderly and younger patients, with no clear age-related difference observed in the incidence of adverse events of ≥grade 3.

papers.abstract_en: Background/Objectives: Leptomeningeal disease (LMD) is among the most severe complications of metastatic breast cancer, with median survival measured in weeks. Definitive diagnosis relies on neuroimaging and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) cytology, which carries a false-negative rate of 40-50% at a single lumbar puncture. Improved tools for detecting and characterizing tumor cells across systemic and central nervous system (CNS) compartments are urgently needed. Methods: We applied an enrichment-free, fluorescence whole-slide imaging (fWSI)-based liquid biopsy platform to ante-mortem and post-mortem peripheral blood (PB) and CSF from five patients with metastatic breast cancer and confirmed or suspected LMD, collected through the City of Hope LEGACY warm autopsy program. Circulating tumor cells (CTCs) were classified by immunophenotype (cytokeratin [CK], vimentin [VIM], CD45/CD31) and morphology. Select cells underwent single-cell copy number variation (CNV) profiling by low-pass whole-genome sequencing. Results: Across 23 samples (11 PB, 12 CSF), we identified marked compartmental heterogeneity in CTC burden, phenotype, and genomic architecture. In the one patient (Patient 1) sampled across all four ventricular-to-cisternal CSF sites, CTC frequency declined from proximal to distal compartments (11.4% in the right lateral ventricle to 0.6% at the foramen magnum), a single-patient observation consistent with a proximal-to-distal gradient. Patients with active, untreated LMD showed high CSF CTC incidence with both epithelial and mesenchymal phenotypes, whereas the two patients receiving intrathecal therapy each showed low or absent CSF CTCs; given the small numbers involved and a plausible technical confound in a third patient, we interpret this association cautiously. Single-cell CNV profiling of CSF-derived CTCs across patients with active LMD revealed highly concordant chromosomal aberration profiles, 100% of CK+ CSF CTCs analyzed carried chromosomal aberrations, consistent with, though not formally establishing, expansion of a genomically evolved subclone within the leptomeningeal compartment; PB-derived cells showed substantially greater heterogeneity. In the two patients with paired post-mortem arterial and venous PB, arterial blood showed higher total rare cell counts in both, and higher CK-positive CTC incidence in one (1425.73 vs. undetectable epi.CTC/mL); the other showed the reverse for this specific metric. Conclusions: Enrichment-free, multi-compartment liquid biopsy reveals a regionally heterogeneous and biologically structured landscape in breast cancer LMD not resolvable by conventional cytology or single-site venous sampling. These findings are consistent with a hypothesis-generating model in which the leptomeningeal space acts as a selective niche for clonally convergent tumor expansion. They also point to the potential of regionally resolved CTC profiling for monitoring LMD treatment response in future, larger cohorts.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Outcomes for patients with osteosarcoma (OS) presenting with metastases at diagnosis or relapsed remain poor with five-year survival rate of only 20-30%. Risk stratification at diagnosis remains limited, and no validated prognostic liquid biopsy analyte currently exists for this disease. OS lacks the recurring mutational hotspots and epithelial surface markers that underpin liquid biopsy strategies developed for carcinomas, necessitating fundamentally different approaches to circulating biomarker detection. METHODS: Peripheral blood samples from 25 pediatric and young adult OS patients at clinically apparent disease timepoints (n = 29 samples) and 76 adult healthy donors (ND) were processed without cell enrichment using fluorescent whole-slide imaging. An outlier detection pipeline employing deep contrastive learned features classified rare cells across eight immunophenotypic categories defined by DAPI, vimentin (V), cytokeratin (CK), and CD45/CD31 (CD) expression. From the same patient cohort, plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA) was analyzed by ichorCNA-based tumor fraction estimation across 42 samples (10 clinically apparent disease timepoints shared with the rare cell cohort and 32 alternative timepoints) from ten patients, and single-cell copy number alteration (scCNA) profiling was performed on 80 rare cells from five patients. RESULTS: Rare cells were detected at a median of approximately 127 cells/mL (range: 29-1114) in OS patients at clinically apparent disease timepoints versus 34 cells/mL (range: 4-225) in healthy donors. DAPI-only (D) cells, identified using a data-driven optimal cutpoint (38.32 cells/mL) that is subject to optimization bias and requires independent validation, were associated with relapse-free survival in this exploratory, single-center OS cohort (log-rank p = 0.0003), with high D cell burden associated with markedly shorter relapse-free survival (median 393 days, 95% CI: 106-572) compared to patients with low D cell counts (median 835 days, 95% CI: 494-1671). D cells also showed the broadest clinical associations, correlating with metastatic burden and disease subgroup. The Vimentin+/CD45- (D|V) population was the strongest discriminator between OS patients and healthy donors (p = 4.64 × 10-12) but did not distinguish relapse-free survival groups within the OS cohort (log-rank p = 0.8367). Genomic analyses at the plasma, single-cell, and tumor tissue levels were largely uninformative. CONCLUSIONS: Enrichment-free rare cell profiling identifies a DAPI-only circulating rare cell population whose abundance is associated with relapse-free survival in this exploratory, single-center OS cohort, accessible by nuclear morphology alone without biomarker enrichment. This is a novel, hypothesis-generating observation that, together with the mesenchymal-forward D|V population characterized here, motivates a larger, independent, prospective validation cohort and dedicated single-cell molecular (proteomic) characterization of the D-cell population, rather than establishing DAPI-only rare cell enumeration as a validated liquid biopsy stratification tool at this stage.

papers.abstract_en: Background/Objectives: Combination chemotherapy remains a cornerstone of breast cancer (BC) treatment, yet the relative contribution of individual drugs within standard regimens remains poorly understood. We investigated whether the activity of the widely used anthracycline-cyclophosphamide-taxane (AC-T) regimen reflects uniform benefit from all constituent drugs or heterogeneous drug-specific vulnerabilities across tumors. Methods: We combined in silico drug-response analyses, functional validation in BC cell lines, and ex vivo profiling in patient-derived organoids (PDOs). Drug responses were integrated into the Probability of Chemotherapeutic Efficacy (PCE), a multidimensional response metric combining relative drug potency, maximal efficacy, and clinically achievable free-drug exposure. To explore the broader applicability of PCE, we additionally applied it to an independent publicly available GR-based pharmacological dataset generated by the HMS LINCS Center. Results: Across BC models, anthracyclines and taxanes displayed only partially overlapping sensitivity profiles, indicating distinct drug-specific vulnerabilities. Functional validation in 2D cell lines and PDOs confirmed highly context-dependent responses to AC-T components. Among 21 PDOs with complete drug-response datasets, extensive interpatient heterogeneity was observed, with non-overlapping patterns of sensitivity to A, C, and T. Responses were better represented as a continuum of functional vulnerability states than as binary sensitive-versus-resistant categories. AC generated the highest proportion of favorable response profiles, with 62% of PDOs classified as partial response-like or complete response-like, compared with 48% for A, 38% for C, and 14% for T. AC activity was positively associated with the most active constituent drug within each PDO. Application of this framework to an independent public dataset produced biologically plausible response patterns consistent with the molecular characteristics of the evaluated breast cancer cell lines, supporting its computational transferability. Conclusions: These findings reveal substantial heterogeneity in the contribution of individual drugs to AC-T activity and are compatible with a model in which different tumors derive benefit from different regimen components. Together, these findings establish a hypothesis-generating functional framework for dissecting the contribution of individual drugs within combination chemotherapy regimens. Prospective studies correlating PDO-derived functional responses with clinical outcomes will be required to determine the predictive value and potential clinical utility of this approach before informing therapeutic decision-making.

papers.abstract_en: Background: This retrospective study introduces imaging inner tumor margin patterns (iITMP) and evaluates their correlation with pathological Worst pattern of invasion (WPOI) in oral tongue squamous cell carcinoma (OTSCC). Associations of iITMP with pathological primary tumor category (pT), histologic grade, perineural invasion (PNI), nodal metastasis, and extranodal extension (ENE) were assessed. Correlations between imaging depth of invasion (iDOI) and pathological DOI (pDOI), and between imaging primary tumor (iT) and pT, PNI, and ENE were evaluated. Methods: Baseline magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) from January 2021 to December 2022 of 224 upfront-operated OTSCC patients was reviewed by two blinded radiologists using contrast-enhanced thin-slice. iITMP (types 1-3) were classified based on inner tumor margin morphology. iDOI was measured after excluding peritumoral hyperenhancement. Correlation between categorical and continuous variables were assessed using Kappa statistics and Spearman's test respectively. Associations between categorical variables were analyzed using Fisher's exact or Pearson's chi-squared tests. Univariable and multivariable analyses were additionally performed. Results: The mean patient age was 47 ± 11 years. Substantial agreement was observed between iITMP and WPOI, and between iT and pT. iDOI strongly correlated with pDOI. iITMP was significantly associated with pT, irregular (iITMP2) and infiltrative (iITMP3) margins were associated with PNI only on univariate analysis, while iITMP was not an independent predictor on multivariable analysis. iT significantly correlated with PNI and ENE. Conclusions: iITMP strongly correlate with WPOI and is substantially associated with pT categories. iT categories show significant association with PNI and ENE. Therefore, iITMP and iT may serve as potential imaging biomarkers of adverse histopathological features in OTSCC.

papers.abstract_en: Background/Objectives: Oral leukoplakia (OL) is a common oral potentially malignant disorder, but prediction of malignant progression remains challenging. This study investigated miR-21-5p and miR-21-3p expression in healthy oral mucosa, OL with epithelial dysplasia, and early oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), together with clinicopathological associations. Methods: Sixty participants were divided into three groups: exposure-free healthy controls (n = 20), histopathologically confirmed OL with epithelial dysplasia (n = 20), and early OSCC (pT1-2N0M0; n = 20). Expression was quantified by RT-qPCR and evaluated using exploratory correlation, regression, Welch's ANOVA, and Games-Howell comparisons. Results: miR-21-5p differed significantly among groups (p < 0.001). Expression was lower in OL than in healthy controls and early OSCC (both p < 0.001), whereas early OSCC and controls did not differ (p = 0.997). miR-21-5p was inversely associated with dysplasia grade (Spearman's ρ = -0.54, p = 0.013; unstandardized regression coefficient B = -0.646, p = 0.017). miR-21-3p was numerically higher in early OSCC, but its overall group difference was not significant (p = 0.051). Conclusions: The two mature miR-21 strands showed distinct, non-linear expression patterns across the three groups. These findings are preliminary and hypothesis-generating; the cross-sectional design does not establish predictive or prognostic value, and validation in larger longitudinal cohorts is required. The unexpected miR-21-5p pattern remains unexplained and requires independent validation.
